# How Config works
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/config/overview

Config levels in Claude for Government: how tenant, directory group, and organization settings combine, what locks do, and when changes reach members.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators and organization owners who set product behavior for the people they manage.

The Config page is where you set product behavior, such as session limits, which products members get, and telemetry, for the people you manage. To open it, go to **Settings > Config** in the admin portal. The same page appears at both the tenant and the organization level, with the same list of settings. For the settings themselves, see [Available settings](/docs/government/config/settings).

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Config essentials" />

Video: Config essentials (2 min 23 s). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

[Transcript](/docs/government/video-walkthroughs#config-essentials)

## How settings are applied

Each setting is resolved through a chain of levels, and a value set at any level becomes the starting point for the levels below it:

1. The Anthropic default
2. Your tenant
3. [Tenant-wide group settings](#group-specific-settings)
4. The organization
5. [Organization group settings](#group-specific-settings)

Expand a setting to see its chain view, which shows the value in effect and where it came from. Settings that may contain secrets, such as telemetry headers, are never echoed back in the chain view. You see that a value is set, but not what it is.

### Setting kinds

Each setting has a fixed kind, which decides how its values combine across the chain:

* A **simple value** is replaced at each level, and the most specific level that set it wins. Most settings work this way, including lists of values such as network hosts, where a lower level's list replaces the one above it.
* A **restriction** is a limit that each level below the tenant can tighten but not loosen from what the levels above it set. The tightest of those values takes effect, except that values set below a [lock](#locks) don't apply. For example, if the tenant sets a session timeout of 30 minutes, an organization can set 15, but a value of 60 has no effect.
* A **collection** accumulates entries from each level. A level can add entries to what the level above provided. Connectors and plugins work this way.

### Locks

A **lock** prevents levels below from changing a setting. To lock a setting on the tenant Config page or at either group level, expand it, choose **Must use this value**, and save. Levels below then see it marked **Locked by** your level and can't change it. Any value a lower level had previously set is ignored while your lock is in place, and it comes back into effect if you later remove the lock.

How far a lock reaches depends on where you set it:

* **On the tenant Config page**, the lock reaches everyone in the tenant. The setting becomes read-only for every organization and at both group levels.
* **On a tenant-wide group setting**, the lock reaches the people that group's settings apply to. They get the locked value even if their organization has set a different one, and organizations cannot set their own value for that group while the lock is in place. Other people in those organizations are not affected.

A group lock does not keep anyone on that group's settings. If someone in the group also belongs to a higher-priority group that has any configuration, that group's settings apply to them instead and the lock does not, as described under [When someone belongs to more than one group](#when-someone-belongs-to-more-than-one-group).

**Locked by Anthropic** means the lock was applied by Anthropic at the application level rather than by your own tenant. It appears on features that are not available in Claude for Government, and only Anthropic can change or unlock those settings.

## Group-specific settings

In addition to setting values for your whole tenant or organization, you can set values for the members of a directory group. A directory group is a group that your identity provider has pushed to Claude for Government over SCIM, as described on the [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access) page.

A group's settings can be tenant-wide or scoped to one organization:

* **Tenant-wide group settings** sit between the tenant and the organization in the chain. Tenant administrators manage these.
* **Organization group settings** are scoped to one organization. A value set here applies only to people who are both a member of the group and a member of that organization, and it is the most specific level in the chain. Organization owners manage these for their own organization and see the same list of groups the tenant does.

To edit settings for a group, choose the group in the scope bar on the Config page, which says whose settings you are editing. Groups appear there once your directory has pushed them. To add connectors for a group's members, see [Who receives a connector](/docs/government/connectors/overview#who-receives-a-connector).

> [!NOTE]
>
> The **Organization instructions** and **Organization Analytics connector** settings can be set at the tenant and organization levels, but not at either group level. Settings that [only a tenant administrator can set](#what-differs-between-the-tenant-and-organization-levels) can't be set for a group.

### Turn a feature on for one group

How you give a feature to one group and nobody else depends on the setting:

* **A simple value, such as Code in Claude Desktop**: turn the feature off on the organization's Config page, then choose the group in the scope bar on that page and turn it on.
* **The switch for a whole product that is off until a level turns it on, such as Claude Code**: leave it unset for the tenant and the organization, and turn it on for the group. An off saved at the tenant or the organization takes priority over the group's on, so [reset](#working-with-the-list) it there first.

To do this for every organization at once, make the same changes on the tenant Config page and choose **Must use this value** for the group, so that an organization's own value can't override it. You can't also lock the feature off for everyone else, because that lock would apply to the group too. An organization can still turn it on for its own members.

### When someone belongs to more than one group

Only one group's settings apply to any given person. When someone is a member of more than one group, the settings from their highest-priority group that has any configuration are used, and the other groups are ignored for that person. A group has configuration for a person once any setting is set or locked for it, either as a tenant-wide group setting or as an organization group setting in that person's organization.

When a higher-priority group gains configuration for someone, it takes the place of the lower-priority group that applied to them before, and the lower-priority group's settings, including locked ones, stop applying to them. Removing a group's last setting, changing the priority order, or changing someone's group memberships in your identity provider can change which group applies to a person in the same way.

A tenant administrator sets the priority order on the [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#directory-groups) page. It cannot be reordered at the organization level.

## What differs between the tenant and organization levels

Almost all settings can be set at either level, with these differences:

* **Some settings can be set only by a tenant administrator.** [Let organizations manage their own seat tiers](/docs/government/config/settings#let-organizations-manage-their-own-seat-tiers) and [Compliance API](/docs/government/config/settings#compliance-api) appear on both pages, but are always read-only at the organization level.
* **Tenant administrators can open any organization's Config page** and act on that organization's behalf, as described under [Config at the tenant level](/docs/government/tenant-admin/configuration). Organization owners see only [their own organization](/docs/government/org-admin/configuration).

## When changes take effect

Settings that govern the admin portal apply immediately. Settings that govern the Claude applications themselves are delivered to each member's application the next time it [refreshes its configuration](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#things-to-know). You do not need to push anything.

Most changes take effect when the member restarts the application. Claude Desktop prompts for that restart, and requires it once the [Restart deadline for configuration changes](/docs/government/config/settings#restart-deadline-for-configuration-changes) has passed. On Claude Desktop 2.2553.0 and later, a few settings take effect in a running application without a restart, such as the **Claude Desktop banner**. The Claude Code command-line tool applies its settings [at startup and on an hourly poll](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#whats-enforced-on-developers).

Changes to the session limits reach members as follows:

* **Session idle timeout**: A shorter session idle timeout applies to new sign-ins immediately. Members who are already signed in move to it within the timeout period their session already had.
* **Maximum session length**: Raising or removing the maximum session length applies to new sign-ins only. Lowering the maximum session length, or setting one for the first time, also reaches members who are already signed in, taking up to one idle timeout period to do so.

## Working with the list

To remove your value and return to whatever the level above provides, expand the setting, select **Reset to default**, and save. Values set at other levels are unaffected and remain in effect once yours is gone.

### Previewing impact

On the tenant Config page, change a setting and select **Preview impact** before you save to see what each organization has now and what it would get. Preview isn't available for settings whose values are hidden for security reasons (for example, settings that can contain authorization tokens).

### Comparing settings across levels

On the Config page, select **Compare config across levels** to see every setting side by side across the full chain.

Type a name into the search box above the table to see what settings apply to that person. Select a row to see how its final value was reached.


# Manage plugins and connectors
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors

Upload plugins in Claude for Government: archive rules, size limits, skills packaged as plugins, the Runs code marker, install behavior, updates, and removal.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators and organization owners who deliver plugins and connectors to the members they manage.

You add plugins on the **Plugins** card and connectors on the **Connectors** card, under **Settings > Config** in the admin portal. The cards themselves are listed under [Integrations](/docs/government/config/settings#integrations) in Available settings.

## Plugins versus connectors

A connector gives Claude access to another service, such as a search tool your agency runs. For adding a connector, see [Connectors](/docs/government/connectors/overview), and for what its tool policy means for members, see [Tool policy](/docs/government/connectors/overview#tool-policy).

A plugin is a package that changes how Claude works. It can add skills, slash commands, and sub-agents, and it can carry [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), which a plugin author sets to run automatically at defined points during a session, such as a command that runs when a session starts. Its hooks run on the member's machine. A plugin can also declare MCP servers of its own, and [Plugins that run code](#plugins-that-run-code) describes how they behave.

## Plugin archive formats

On the **Config** page, open the **Plugins** card, click **Add plugins**, and drop the zip. The preview shows the plugin's name, version, description, and any [**Runs code**](#plugins-that-run-code) marker. For one plugin, choose its [install behavior](#install-behavior). The add button saves at once.

The **Plugins** card accepts a single `.zip` file. The file can be one plugin package or a marketplace archive that holds several plugins, such as the downloaded ZIP of a repository that publishes a set of plugins. A single plugin package can be up to 10 MB, and a marketplace archive can be up to 15 MB. A plugin package can hold up to 50 MB of uncompressed content, whether you upload it on its own or inside a marketplace archive.

From a marketplace archive you select which plugins to add:

* **Plugins hosted elsewhere**: Only plugins whose files are packaged inside the archive are added, so an entry in the marketplace listing that points to a plugin hosted elsewhere is skipped.
* **Layout**: In a marketplace archive, each plugin sits in its own subdirectory, and the marketplace listing points at those subdirectories. A listing entry whose source is the archive root itself, `./`, is not supported and adds nothing, so for a repository laid out as a single plugin with its own marketplace file, remove the marketplace file and upload it as one plugin.

### What a plugin archive can contain

A plugin package is laid out around a manifest at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. The [plugins reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference) describes the general plugin format. Claude for Government accepts the narrower set described here, so a package that follows only the general reference can be rejected.

* **Manifest**: The manifest is a JSON object, saved as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark. `name` and `version` are required. `name` becomes the plugin's identity everywhere it appears, in lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, up to 64 characters and starting with a letter or digit. Add a short `description`.
* **Folders**: Content sits in a fixed set of folders, all lowercase and case-sensitive: `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/`, `hooks/`, and `monitors/`, plus `.claude-plugin/` for the manifest and an optional `icon.png`. `commands/` and `agents/` take `.md` files, `hooks/` and `monitors/` take `.json` files, and `skills/` takes text files in these formats: `.md`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.csv`.
* **Other files**: The root can also hold files such as `README.md`, `LICENSE`, and `CONNECTORS.md`. Other text files in those formats, at the root or in folders of your own, are accepted. Any other file type, anywhere in the package, is rejected.
* **Text only**: Apart from the optional icon, everything in a package must be text in UTF-8.
* **Names**: File and folder names must be ASCII. Nothing in the package may start with a dot apart from `.claude-plugin/` and a root `.mcp.json`: repository files such as `.github/` or `.gitattributes` must be left out, while `.gitignore`, `.DS_Store`, and Apple's `__MACOSX/` folders are dropped for you.
* **Zip paths**: Paths inside the zip must use forward slashes. File Explorer's **Compress to ZIP file** writes them, while Windows PowerShell 5.1's `Compress-Archive` can write backslash paths, which the upload rejects. A zip that wraps everything in one top folder, which is what zipping the plugin folder or downloading a repository as a ZIP produces, works, as long as the plugin holds no other dot-prefixed files.

### Package a skill as a plugin

To distribute skills to members, bundle them in a plugin. The smallest valid package is the manifest plus your skill folder under `skills/`:

```text theme={null}
acme-skills.zip
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json
└── skills/
    └── brand-guidelines/
        ├── SKILL.md
        └── palette.csv
```

Here `plugin.json` can be `{"name": "acme-skills", "version": "1.0.0", "description": "Agency writing skills"}`. Inside `skills/`, each skill is one folder holding a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter carries a `description` and a `name` that matches the folder name, with any reference files beside it. One plugin can carry several skills, one folder per skill. The [skill authoring guide](/docs/skills/how-to) covers the format, but an upload that contains the scripts or binary assets it describes is rejected. [What a plugin archive can contain](#what-a-plugin-archive-can-contain) has the full rules.

A bare skill archive, such as a zip of the skill folder alone or a `.skill` file from [Claude Desktop](/docs/government/desktop/skills), which is a zip of the bare skill folder, is not a plugin: add the manifest and move the folder under `skills/` to convert it.

The upload checks packaging, not skill content. After [adding the plugin](#plugin-archive-formats), open Claude Desktop as a member: install the plugin if you chose [**Members choose**](#install-behavior), then give Claude a task the skill should match and confirm Claude picks it up.

## Plugins that run code

A **Runs code** marker in the upload preview warns that the plugin can run code on the member's machine, for example through hooks or an MCP server. You confirm that you trust a marked package before it is added, and for a marketplace archive one confirmation covers every marked plugin in the batch. After you add it, the plugin's row on the **Plugins** card keeps the marker. You are responsible for the plugins you distribute to members, so read each plugin's contents before you upload it, marked or not.

Claude Desktop can run a local MCP server that the plugin declares on the member's machine, or connect to a remote one. If the server does not start or connect, check [**Let members add their own connectors**](/docs/government/config/settings#let-members-add-their-own-connectors), [**Member-added connectors**](/docs/government/config/settings#member-added-connectors), and [**Blocked connectors**](/docs/government/config/settings#blocked-connectors).

## Install behavior

Each plugin on the **Plugins** card has an install behavior. To change it, set it on the plugin's row and save the change. **Auto-install** installs the plugin on every member's Claude Desktop without the member doing anything. **Members choose** offers the plugin to members, who install it themselves from their organization's plugins in Claude Desktop, as described in [Plugins in Claude Desktop](/docs/government/desktop/plugins). Plugins you add from a marketplace archive start as **Members choose**.

Claude Desktop syncs your organization's plugin list when it starts and periodically while it runs, so you do not need to push anything. A member can remove a plugin you installed automatically, and it stays removed on the device where they removed it.

**Let members add plugin marketplaces** and **Let members add their own plugins** control whether members can also add plugins of their own, as described under [Integrations](/docs/government/config/settings#member-added-plugins-and-marketplaces) in Available settings. Both are off by default. Plugins that members add are separate from the ones you add and do not appear on the **Plugins** card.

## Where plugins are added

Plugins are added at the tenant or organization level. Plugins the tenant adds flow to every organization and appear on each organization's **Plugins** card under **From levels above**. A plugin an organization adds with the same name takes priority over the tenant's for that organization's members.

A tenant administrator can lock the plugin list, under **Advanced: raw configuration** on the card, which makes it read-only for organizations, following the lock behavior in [How Config works](/docs/government/config/overview#locks).

## Update or remove a plugin

To update a plugin, go to **Settings > Config**, open the **Plugins** card, click **Add plugins**, and upload the new version's archive. An archive whose manifest `name` matches a plugin you already added replaces that plugin, whatever the two versions say, and members who have the plugin receive the new version automatically. Give each upload a new `version`, so that older Claude Desktop versions pick it up. To refresh the plugins you added from a marketplace archive, upload a new version of it with the same **Tag**, which the preview fills in from the marketplace's name. Plugins under that tag that the new archive lacks are removed unless you choose in the preview to keep them.

To remove a plugin, click its remove icon and save the change. Claude for Government stops delivering the plugin, and Claude Desktop removes it for members who have it the next time it [syncs your organization's plugin list](#install-behavior). After that sync the plugin's hooks no longer run. A new chat cannot use the plugin's skills or commands, but a chat the member was using at the time can still use them. Claude Desktop versions earlier than 1.46388.1 keep the plugin, hooks included, until the member removes it.


# Available settings
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/config/settings

Config page settings in Claude for Government, such as session timeouts, network and folder access, tool approvals, connectors, plugins, telemetry, and updates.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators and organization owners who set product behavior for the people they manage.

Find each setting on the **Config** page in the admin portal under its category in that page's sidebar. Each setting can be set at both the tenant and organization level unless noted otherwise. To set a value for a directory group, see [Group-specific settings](/docs/government/config/overview#group-specific-settings). For how the levels combine, what locking does, when a change reaches members, and how to compare and preview, see [How Config works](/docs/government/config/overview).

Where **Applies to** gives a version, earlier versions ignore the setting. The **Config** page can show settings that are not listed here.

## Product availability

| Setting | What it does | Default | Applies to |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Claude Desktop** | Makes Claude Desktop available. | On | Claude Desktop |
| **Claude Desktop home** | Chooses what members see in Claude Desktop: **Standard** (Chat and Cowork combined), **Simple** (Chat), **Chat only** (Chat without Advanced file analysis), or **Off** (Code only). **Separate settings** leaves it to the Chat, file analysis, and Cowork switches. Any other choice your agency makes overrides them, unless a level above has locked one. | Set by Anthropic | Claude Desktop 1.52386.0 or later |
| **Chat in Claude Desktop** | Lets members chat with Claude in Claude Desktop, for quick questions and drafting. Without Chat, members cannot open their existing chats. | On | Claude Desktop |
| **Advanced file analysis in Chat** | Lets Claude run code in a sandbox for data analysis in Chat. Only takes effect where **Shell commands** and **Chat in Claude Desktop** are both on. Without this setting, Claude cannot read Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files that members attach in Chat. | On | Claude Desktop |
| **Cowork in Claude Desktop** | Lets members give Claude longer tasks, such as research, analysis, and drafting documents, which it works through on its own in Claude Desktop. Without Cowork, members cannot continue their Cowork tasks. Claude Desktop versions earlier than 1.30096.1 can still show Cowork while it is off, but do not run its tasks. | On | Claude Desktop |
| **Code in Claude Desktop** | Lets members use Claude Code inside Claude Desktop to write and run code. Without Code, members cannot open their existing Code sessions. | On | Claude Desktop |
| **Scheduled tasks** | Lets members set up [tasks that Claude runs on a schedule](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#scheduledtasksenabled). Turning it off also turns off scheduling in Claude Code, such as `/loop`. | On | Claude Desktop 2.110.0 or later, Claude Code |
| **Claude Code** | Makes the [Claude Code command-line tool](/docs/government/deploy-claude-code/configure) available. | Off | Claude Code |
| **Claude for Microsoft 365** | Makes [Claude for Microsoft 365](/docs/government/deploy-microsoft-365/configure), the add-in for Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, available. | Off | Claude for Microsoft 365 |

Turning off **Claude Desktop**, **Claude Code**, or **Claude for Microsoft 365** stops the members the setting applies to from using that application. An organization cannot turn on a product that the tenant has turned off. These switches turn applications off, not accounts, and are not a security boundary: to cut one member off from everything at once, deactivate their account (see [Deactivated users](/docs/government/org-admin/users#deactivated-users)).

From November 10, 2026, members whose settings give them Cowork get the [**Standard** home](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/unified-claude#what-users-see-with-unified-claude) in Claude Desktop 4.29.0 or later: turning off Chat or Advanced file analysis has no effect for them. To change the home, use the **Config** page, not `desktopHome` in a device management profile.

## Sessions and access

| Setting | What it does | Default | Applies to |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Session idle timeout** | How long a member can stay inactive before being signed out, from 15 to 5,760 minutes (96 hours). An organization's or group's value longer than the tenant's has no effect. | 1,440 minutes (24 hours) | All products |
| **Maximum session length** | The longest a member can stay signed in, even while active, before they have to sign in again, from 60 to 525,600 minutes (365 days). Each level can set or shorten the maximum but not lengthen it past what the level above allows. | No maximum | All products |
| [**Allowed network hosts**](#allowed-network-hosts) | A list of hostnames that tools may reach, for example to install packages or fetch web pages. | **Claude connection only** | Claude Desktop, Claude Code |
| **IPv6 in the sandbox** | Lets tools in the sandbox [reach IPv6-only hosts](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#coworkvmipv6enabled) through the computer's own IPv6 connection. **Allowed network hosts** still applies. | Off | Claude Desktop 1.52386.0 or later on macOS and Windows |
| [**Allowed workspace folders**](#allowed-workspace-folders) | Which folders members can pick as a project folder in Claude Desktop. | **Any folder** | Claude Desktop |
| **Block reads outside workspace folders** | Stops Claude's file tools in Code sessions in Claude Desktop from reading files outside the session's project folder and any folders listed in **Allowed workspace folders**. Its effect on the shell commands Claude runs [differs by operating system](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/code#applied-as-managed-policy). | Off | Claude Desktop 1.46388.1 or later |
| **Attach files to chat**, on the **Microsoft 365 features** card | Lets members attach files to chat by picking, dragging, or pasting them. | On | Claude for Microsoft 365 |
| **Accept all edits**, on the **Microsoft 365 features** card | Lets members switch to **Accept all edits**, where Claude makes most edits to the open file without asking. Turning it off also turns off **Skip all permissions**. | On | Claude for Microsoft 365 |
| **File access rules (Microsoft 365)** | Rules that block Claude on files with chosen Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels, or block attaching them. On a blocked file, members see "Claude is unavailable for this document". A rule can **Block** matching files or **Allow only matching files**. If the add-in cannot read a file's label, the file counts as blocked for every feature that has a rule covering it. | None | Claude for Microsoft 365 |
| **Request headers (Claude for Microsoft 365)** | Extra headers Claude for Microsoft 365 sends with each request to Claude. Each member's add-in receives them. Headers are hidden after you save them. | None | Claude for Microsoft 365 |

**Maximum session length** always counts from when the member originally signed in, so a session that is already older than the new maximum ends when it [picks up the change](/docs/government/config/overview#when-changes-take-effect) and the member is prompted to sign in again. Your identity provider decides whether that sign-in asks the member to authenticate again or passes them straight through.

### Allowed network hosts

The list covers [web fetch and shell commands](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#coworkegressallowedhosts) in Chat and Cowork, the [sandboxed shell commands](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#code-in-claude-desktop) of Code sessions on macOS and Linux, and those of the Claude Code command-line tool while [**Shell command sandbox**](#shell-command-sandbox) is **On**. Web search, connectors, and the app's own connections do not use this list.

Entries are hostnames or wildcard patterns such as `*.example.com`, not IP addresses or ports, and match by name, not by the address a name resolves to. Claude Desktop ignores a wildcard for a top-level domain such as `*.gov`, so list each domain and its subdomains, as in `example.gov` and `*.example.gov`. The list holds up to 200 entries, including each hostname that **Add package registries** adds. **Allow all** adds `*`, which allows every host. On macOS and Linux, Claude Desktop then does not turn on the [sandbox](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#code-in-claude-desktop) for shell commands in Code sessions while [**Allowed workspace folders**](#allowed-workspace-folders) is **Any folder**, its default.

### Allowed workspace folders

Check **Block all workspace folders** to allow none, in which case Claude can still work in Chat and Cowork in folders it creates inside its own sandbox. Subfolders of a listed folder are included. The setting does not stop the shell commands Claude runs in a Code session from reading files elsewhere on the device, and [Code in Claude Desktop](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#code-in-claude-desktop) describes what confines those commands on each operating system.

* **Windows and Mac**: a list with only Windows entries leaves Mac users with no allowed folder, so include a Mac path as well, or one that starts with `~`, which stands for each member's home folder on both Windows and Mac.
* **Synced folders**: on Windows, `~/Documents` refers to the local Documents folder in the user profile, not one redirected to OneDrive. For that one, use [a variable](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#allowedworkspacefolders) such as `%OneDriveCommercial%` or `%OneDrive%`. For Code sessions and other work that creates many files, consider listing a local folder that is not synced, such as `~/ClaudeWork`.

## Claude Code

Claude for Government delivers these settings to the command-line tool after a member signs in, and in Claude Desktop 2.9939.2 or later they can also reach Code sessions. While Claude Code is in [early access](/docs/government/deploy-claude-code/configure), the section appears once your agency has access.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Applies to |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Blocked shell commands** | Command names, such as `curl` or `ssh`, that Claude Code applies as [deny rules](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#bash) for its Bash and PowerShell tools. | None blocked | Claude Code |
| **Managed hooks** | [Hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) that run in every member's Claude Code sessions, such as a command that writes an audit record after a tool use. | None | Claude Code |
| **Member-added hooks** | Whether hooks and custom status lines that members set up in their own or their projects' settings run as well. Managed hooks still run, and in Claude Desktop so do hooks inside plugins. | **Blocked** | Claude Code |
| **Plugin sources** | Which [marketplaces](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/org#restrict-what-users-can-install) members can install Claude Code plugins from, one of **None**, **Approved sources only** with an **Approved plugin sources** list, or **Any source** with a **Blocked plugin sources** list. | **None** | Claude Code |
| **Sideloaded plugins** | Whether members can load plugins, agents, or connector files with a command-line flag. | **Blocked** | Claude Code command-line tool |
| **Minimum Claude Code version** | Claude Code below this version does not start and tells the member to update. | No minimum | Claude Code |
| **Maximum Claude Code version** | Claude Code above this version does not start. | No maximum | Claude Code command-line tool |
| **Opening from the browser** | Whether Claude Code sets itself up to open from links in web pages and editors, with a prompt filled in. | **Blocked** | Claude Code |
| **Shell command sandbox** | Turns [Claude Code's sandbox](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#code-in-claude-desktop) on or off. **On** takes effect in the command-line tool on macOS, Linux, and WSL devices that can run the sandbox, and holds sandboxed shell commands to [**Allowed network hosts**](#allowed-network-hosts). On a device that cannot run the sandbox, shell commands can run outside it. | **Left to the device** | Claude Code |

Two switches under [Integrations](#integrations) narrow **Any source**: while **Let members add plugin marketplaces** is off, members install only from marketplaces the **Approved plugin sources** list allows, and while **Let members add their own plugins** is off, they cannot add their own marketplace from a file or folder on their machine.

Settings in other categories govern Claude Code too, such as **Scheduled tasks** under [Product availability](#product-availability) and **Member-added connectors** under [Integrations](#integrations).

## Claude behavior

| Setting | What it does | Default | Applies to |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Organization instructions** | Instructions Claude follows for everyone in your organization, in every product. | None | All products |

Organization instructions guide how Claude responds, and they are not an enforced restriction. Members do not see the instructions in their applications. Instructions set at the organization level replace the tenant's instructions for that organization rather than adding to them. A change takes effect from each member's next message.

## Compliance and telemetry

These settings cover usage telemetry export to your own collector and Claude Desktop updates.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Applies to |
| - | - | - | - |
| [**Telemetry endpoint**](#telemetry-endpoint) | The base address of your [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) collector, such as `https://otel-collector.example.gov:4318`. Each product adds its own paths and sends OTLP over HTTP, not gRPC, directly from members' devices, so the collector must be reachable from their networks. | Empty, which turns telemetry off | All products |
| **Telemetry headers** | Headers each product sends with every telemetry request, such as an Authorization header carrying your collector's token. Each member's app receives these headers and sends its telemetry directly, so use a credential that can only send data to your collector. | None | All products |
| **Telemetry content capture** | [Content](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/telemetry#content-capture) each product adds to the telemetry it sends to your collector: **Prompts**, **Claude's responses**, **Tool inputs**, **Tool results**, and **Full requests and responses**. Captured content goes only to your collector and is never sent to Anthropic. | No content captured | All products |
| **Application event level (Claude Desktop)** | How much of [Claude Desktop's own event log](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#otlpdesktoploglevel) is sent to your collector, in addition to usage telemetry: **Off**, **Errors only**, **Warnings and errors**, **Informational**, or **Debug**. | **Errors only** | Claude Desktop |
| **Telemetry resource attributes** | Labels added to every telemetry record each product sends, such as your agency or environment name, so your collector can tell where each record comes from. | Not set | All products |
| **Telemetry traces** (beta) | Adds [traces](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/telemetry#traces-beta), so that the events of one request can be followed together. Traces carry message and tool content only for the categories selected in **Telemetry content capture**. | Off | All products; Claude Desktop 1.22209.0 or later |
| **Block automatic updates** | Stops Claude Desktop from downloading and installing updates automatically. Turn this on only if your organization distributes Claude Desktop updates itself. For devices where no member is signed in, and for Linux, see [Automatic updates](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#automatic-updates). | Off | Claude Desktop on macOS and Windows |
| **Restart deadline for updates** | How long a downloaded update can wait before Claude Desktop restarts to install it, from 1 to 72 hours. | [Claude Desktop's default](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#autoupdaterenforcementhours) | Claude Desktop |
| **Restart deadline for configuration changes** | How long a member can put off restarting Claude Desktop after the app detects a configuration change, from 0 to 336 hours (14 days). | [Claude Desktop's default](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#relaunchenforcementhours) | Claude Desktop 1.40609.0 or later |

* **Telemetry headers**: the headers you enter replace all of the saved ones when you save, so enter every header again when you add or change one.
* **Telemetry content capture**: **Tool results** adds tool output only while **Telemetry traces** is on. **Full requests and responses** can carry tool output with traces on or off.
* **Application event level (Claude Desktop)**: at **Informational** and **Debug**, the application events also include each conversation's title, and the title text is sent only when **Prompts** is selected in **Telemetry content capture**.
* **Telemetry resource attributes**: a list set at an organization or group replaces the inherited list, so repeat any attributes that should still apply.

### Telemetry endpoint

Once a member has signed in and the app has loaded their configuration from Claude for Government, it takes its telemetry settings from that configuration alone and ignores any set on the device itself. Claude Desktop keeps working when the collector refuses requests or cannot be reached, and members see no error. For what the collector must accept, and how to confirm that telemetry is arriving, see [Collector endpoint and headers](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/telemetry#collector-endpoint-and-headers). For Claude for Microsoft 365, the collector must also accept [cross-origin requests from your Claude for Government host](/docs/government/deploy-microsoft-365/configure#before-you-begin).

Each record [identifies the member](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/telemetry#user-attribution). See what [Claude Desktop](/docs/cowork/monitoring#events), [Claude for Microsoft 365](/docs/office-agents/opentelemetry#what-the-collector-receives), and [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage) send.

## Admin Console

| Setting | What it does | Default | Applies to |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Let organizations manage their own seat tiers** | Lets organization owners create and edit self-managed seat tiers on the [Tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) page, in addition to the Anthropic-managed ones. When it is off, the **Reset usage limits** action on the [Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users) page is also unavailable. | On | Admin Console |
| **Compliance API** | Controls whether the [Compliance API](/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api) is available. When this is off, requests are refused and existing keys stay listed so you can revoke them. | On | Admin Console |

# Set up the Microsoft 365 connector
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/connectors/microsoft-365

Register a Microsoft Entra application for the Microsoft 365 connector in Claude Desktop, choose its read and write permissions, and fix sign-in errors.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners and tenant administrators who want Claude to reach their agency's Microsoft 365 content, and who can register an application in Microsoft Entra ID (or can work with someone who can).

The Microsoft 365 connector lets Claude Desktop read and search your agency's Outlook mail, calendar, and OneDrive and SharePoint files, and read Teams chats. The connector runs locally on each member's machine: when a member signs in with their own Microsoft account, Claude Desktop calls Microsoft Graph directly from their device, so those calls and the member's sign-in tokens stay between their device and Microsoft and never pass through any Anthropic service. What Claude reads into a conversation is then handled like anything else the member sends to Claude.

Because each member signs in individually, Claude can only reach content that the signed-in member can already open in Microsoft 365. Your existing Microsoft 365 permissions, sharing rules, and Conditional Access policies apply unchanged.

First, someone with administrator access in Microsoft Entra ID registers an application in your Microsoft tenant. Then you enter that application's details on the **Microsoft 365** card on the [Config](/docs/government/org-admin/configuration) page. Claude for Microsoft 365, the add-in for Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, is a separate product with [its own setup](/docs/government/deploy-microsoft-365/configure).

## Before you start

You need someone with the **Cloud Application Administrator**, **Application Administrator**, or **Global Administrator** role in your Microsoft Entra tenant. That person registers the application and approves the Microsoft Graph permissions for your whole tenant. If that isn't you, send them the [Register an application in Microsoft Entra](#register-an-application-in-microsoft-entra) section below and the permissions you plan to select under [**Access**](#choose-which-microsoft-365-permissions-to-allow); you can fill in the Config page form once they send you the two IDs and tell you which Microsoft cloud the tenant is in.

## Register an application in Microsoft Entra

For the portal screens in more detail, see the first step of [Set up the local connector](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/connectors-m365#set-up-the-local-connector) in the Claude Desktop documentation.

Microsoft 365 GCC (the standard Government Community Cloud) uses the commercial Microsoft Entra service, so follow the steps below unchanged and leave **Azure cloud** set to **Commercial** when you [configure the connector on the Config page](#configure-the-connector-on-the-config-page).

GCC High and DoD tenants use the Azure Government cloud instead. Register the application at `https://entra.microsoft.us` (or `https://portal.azure.us`) rather than `entra.microsoft.com`, and select the matching **Azure cloud** value when you [configure the connector on the Config page](#configure-the-connector-on-the-config-page).

**1. Create the app registration**

1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), open **App registrations** from the left navigation and select **+ New registration**.
2. Under **Supported account types**, choose **Single tenant only - \{your organization}**. Older versions of the portal label this option **Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single tenant)**.
3. Leave **Redirect URI** blank for now, and select **Register**.

**2. Add the redirect URIs**

On the **Authentication** page, add these three redirect URIs under **Mobile and desktop applications** (the Windows, UWP, and Console card, not the iOS/macOS card). Replace `APPLICATION_CLIENT_ID` with the **Application (client) ID** shown on the application's Overview page.

```text theme={null}
http://localhost
ms-appx-web://Microsoft.AAD.BrokerPlugin/APPLICATION_CLIENT_ID
msauth.com.anthropic.claudefordesktop://auth
```

The `http://localhost` URI is the standard loopback redirect for browser sign-in. When a member signs in through their browser, Microsoft Entra sends the response to a temporary listener on the member's own machine, so it never leaves the device. The other two URIs let Claude Desktop sign in through the operating system's account broker on Windows and macOS devices that meet the [brokered sign-in requirements](#brokered-sign-in-requirements). Brokered sign-in carries the device-identity claim that Conditional Access policies such as **Require compliant device** evaluate, so register all three now even if you are not sure you need them.

> [!NOTE]
>
> All three URIs must be under **Mobile and desktop applications**, not **Web**. After you save, Entra may display the `msauth.com.anthropic.claudefordesktop://auth` URI under a separate **iOS/macOS** section. That's expected, since both sections are public-client platforms. To double-check, open **Manage > Manifest** and confirm the three URIs appear under `publicClient.redirectUris` rather than `web.redirectUris`. If the list also contains `msauth.com.anthropic.claudefordesktop.helper://auth`, remove that entry. Claude Desktop does not use it.

**3. Allow public client flows**

Still under **Authentication**, set **Allow public client flows** to **Yes**, and select **Save**. Claude Desktop signs in as a public client with no client secret, and with this setting off, brokered sign-in on managed devices fails with Entra error `AADSTS7000218`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Setting **Allow public client flows** to **Yes** also permits the device-code sign-in flow, which attackers can abuse for phishing. To close that path, apply a tenant Conditional Access policy that blocks the device-code authentication flow. Scope the policy to **All resources**, not to this app registration, because Conditional Access evaluates the resource a token is requested for rather than the requesting client.

**4. Add and approve Microsoft Graph permissions**

Under **API permissions**, add these **Microsoft Graph** **Delegated permissions**, then select **Grant admin consent for \{your tenant name}** and confirm.

* `User.Read` (under **User**) and `offline_access` (under **OpenId permissions**). The connector always requests these two at sign-in, so they must be approved regardless of what you select under **Access** later.
* Every permission you plan to select under **Access** on the Config page. The eight Default permissions (`Mail.Read`, `Mail.Read.Shared`, `Calendars.Read`, `Calendars.Read.Shared`, `Files.Read.All`, `Sites.Read.All`, `Chat.Read`, `OnlineMeetings.Read`) are pre-selected there. See [Choose which Microsoft 365 permissions to allow](#choose-which-microsoft-365-permissions-to-allow) for what each one does.

The **Grant admin consent** step approves these permissions once for every member of your Microsoft tenant, so individual members are not asked to approve them again when they sign in. Until you complete this step, members see Entra error `AADSTS65001` at sign-in (or, on tenants that allow members to approve permissions themselves, a per-member consent prompt).

> [!NOTE]
>
> A delegated permission lets the application act on a member's behalf, limited to whatever that member can already do. It does not let Claude see content the member cannot see. For example, granting `Files.Read.All` lets Claude read files the signed-in member can open, not every file in your tenant.

**5. Copy the two IDs**

On the application's **Overview** page, copy the **Application (client) ID** and the **Directory (tenant) ID**.

### Allow outbound network access

The connector calls Microsoft directly from each member's device, so devices need outbound HTTPS access to the Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Graph hosts for your cloud.

| Azure cloud | Sign-in host | Microsoft Graph host |
| - | - | - |
| Commercial | `login.microsoftonline.com` | `graph.microsoft.com` |
| US Government GCC-High | `login.microsoftonline.us` | `graph.microsoft.us` |
| US Government DoD | `login.microsoftonline.us` | `dod-graph.microsoft.us` |

Downloads of OneDrive and SharePoint files also need access to your Microsoft tenant's SharePoint and OneDrive hosts. For Office documents, see the network hosts step of [Set up the local connector](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/connectors-m365#set-up-the-local-connector) in the Claude Desktop documentation.

No outbound access to any Anthropic host is needed for the connector's Microsoft 365 calls.

## Configure the connector on the Config page

On the [Config](/docs/government/org-admin/configuration) page, select the **Integrations** category, expand the **Microsoft 365** card, and fill in the form.

| Field | What to enter |
| - | - |
| **Tenant ID** | The **Directory (tenant) ID** from the application's Overview page. |
| **Client ID** | The **Application (client) ID** from the application's Overview page. |
| **Azure cloud** | **Commercial** for most tenants, including Microsoft 365 GCC. Choose **US Government GCC-High** or **US Government DoD** only if your Microsoft tenant is in one of those clouds. |
| **Access** | See [Choose which Microsoft 365 permissions to allow](#choose-which-microsoft-365-permissions-to-allow). |

Save the card. The connector reaches each member's Claude Desktop the next time it starts or the member signs in to Claude for Government. To turn the connector off, clear both **Tenant ID** and **Client ID** and save the card at each level where it is set. Members who already have Claude Desktop open keep the connector until [the app relaunches](/docs/government/config/overview#when-changes-take-effect).

## Choose which Microsoft 365 permissions to allow

The **Access** picker controls which Microsoft Graph delegated permissions Claude Desktop requests when a member signs in. The permissions marked **Default** below are already selected when you first open the card and give read-only access to the member's mail, calendar, files, sites, Teams chat, and online meetings. At least one permission must be selected.

Whatever you select here must also be added and approved on the Entra app registration (step 4 above).

* You can approve read broadly while limiting write to specific services or none at all by selecting only the permissions you want.
* The **Access** selection applies to everyone who receives this connector card. To give different groups different permissions, set the card at the group scope on the Config page; see [Group-specific settings](/docs/government/config/overview#group-specific-settings).

### Read access

| Permission | What it lets Claude do |
| - | - |
| `Mail.Read` (Default) | Read the member's mail |
| `Mail.Read.Shared` (Default) | Read mail in mailboxes shared with the member |
| `Calendars.Read` (Default) | Read the member's calendar events |
| `Calendars.Read.Shared` (Default) | Read events on calendars shared with the member and find free meeting times |
| `Files.Read.All` (Default) | Read files the member can open in OneDrive and SharePoint |
| `Sites.Read.All` (Default) | Read SharePoint site content the member can open |
| `Chat.Read` (Default) | Read the member's Teams chats |
| `OnlineMeetings.Read` (Default) | Read the member's online meetings |
| `MailboxSettings.Read` | Read the member's mailbox time zone so that dates in requests follow the member's local time rather than UTC |
| `People.Read` | Search for people by name or email address |
| `Team.ReadBasic.All` | List the member's teams in Microsoft Teams |
| `Channel.ReadBasic.All` | List the channels in the member's teams |

### Read access requiring administrator approval

These two permissions always require the **Grant admin consent** step in Entra, regardless of your tenant's user-consent policy. Until that step is done, sign-in fails for every member when either permission is requested.

| Permission | What it lets Claude do |
| - | - |
| `ChannelMessage.Read.All` | Search messages in the member's Teams chats and channels and, on Claude Desktop 1.49585.0 or later, read channel messages. Without it, `Chat.Read` still lets Claude list and read the member's chats. |
| `OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All` | Read meeting transcripts |

### Write access

Write permissions let Claude take actions in Microsoft 365 on the member's behalf, such as sending mail, creating calendar events, and editing files. Members approve each write action in Claude Desktop before it runs. The connector is read-only unless you select at least one of these.

| Permission | What it lets Claude do |
| - | - |
| `Mail.Send` | Send mail, send drafts, and forward mail on the member's behalf. Forwarding and sending drafts also use a mail read permission (any of `Mail.Read`, `Mail.Read.Shared`, or `Mail.ReadWrite`) for pre-send checks. |
| `Mail.ReadWrite` | Create, edit, and delete drafts; trash, restore, and delete messages; apply and remove labels on messages |
| `Calendars.ReadWrite` | Create, update, delete, and respond to calendar events |
| `Files.ReadWrite.All` | Create, edit, rename, move, copy, and delete files and folders the member can edit in OneDrive and SharePoint |
| `Sites.ReadWrite.All` | Additional SharePoint write access beyond files. No Claude action requires this permission; `Files.ReadWrite.All` covers file actions in both OneDrive and SharePoint. |
| `ChatMessage.Send` | Send messages in the member's existing Teams chats |
| `ChannelMessage.Send` | Post messages to Teams channels |
| `Chat.Create` | Start new Teams chats |
| `MailboxSettings.ReadWrite` | Create and delete the member's mail rules, manage labels, and configure automatic replies |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Removing a permission from the **Access** picker changes what Claude Desktop requests the next time a member signs in, but it does not revoke permissions that Microsoft Entra has already approved for the application. To revoke a permission entirely, remove it in the Entra admin center under **Enterprise applications** > your application > **Permissions**.

## What members see

After you save the card, **Microsoft 365** appears under **Customize > Connectors** in each member's Claude Desktop. The member selects **Connect** and signs in with their Microsoft work account. On devices that meet the brokered sign-in requirements below, this opens the operating system's account picker; otherwise, it opens the default browser.

Sign-in tokens are stored encrypted on the member's device and persist across restarts, so members are not asked to sign in again each session. Selecting **Disconnect** deletes the connector's stored tokens from the device. On the brokered sign-in path, the device's work or school account is managed by the operating system and remains after Disconnect, and selecting **Connect** again shows the account picker. To end a member's access entirely, revoke the member's sessions in the Entra admin center or, on the brokered sign-in path, remove the account from the device in Windows Settings (**Accounts > Access work or school**) or macOS Company Portal. On Claude Desktop 1.49585.0 or later, revocation takes effect within minutes where Microsoft's [Continuous Access Evaluation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-continuous-access-evaluation) applies. Otherwise, it takes effect once the member's current access token expires.

### Brokered sign-in requirements

If your Conditional Access policies require a compliant or managed device, sign-in must carry a device-identity claim. Brokered sign-in provides that claim directly; browser sign-in provides it only when the browser itself is integrated with device identity (for example, Microsoft Edge signed in with the work account on an Entra-joined Windows device, or a macOS browser with the Enterprise SSO integration deployed).

Brokered sign-in requires the broker redirect URIs from step 2, **Allow public client flows** set to **Yes** (step 3), and the following on each device:

| Platform | Broker availability requirements |
| - | - |
| Windows | The device is joined or registered to Entra ID (Entra joined, Entra hybrid joined, or Entra registered). |
| macOS | The Mac is enrolled in device management and registered in Entra ID. **Intune Company Portal** is installed, and an **Extensible SSO** configuration profile of type **Redirect** pointed at the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in is deployed through device management. |

When the broker is unavailable, Claude Desktop falls back to browser sign-in automatically.

## Common problems

| What the member sees | What it means | How to fix it |
| - | - | - |
| **Microsoft 365** is missing from the member's Claude Desktop | The connector is off for the member until a **Microsoft 365** card with a **Tenant ID** and a **Client ID** is in effect for them. | [Fill in the card](#configure-the-connector-on-the-config-page), then restart Claude Desktop. If it is still missing, [look the member up](/docs/government/config/overview#comparing-settings-across-levels) to see which level's card they get. |
| Entra error `AADSTS50011` at sign-in | One of the redirect URIs from step 2 is missing from the app registration, was entered with a different value, or was added under the **Web** platform instead of **Mobile and desktop applications**. The error message names the URI that Claude Desktop sent. | Compare it with step 2 and add or correct that URI under **Mobile and desktop applications**. |
| Entra error `AADSTS900971` at sign-in on macOS | No redirect URI is registered for macOS brokered sign-in. | Add `msauth.com.anthropic.claudefordesktop://auth` under **Mobile and desktop applications** (step 2). |
| Entra error `AADSTS65001` at sign-in, or a Microsoft consent prompt even though you selected **Grant admin consent** | The Microsoft Graph permissions have not been approved for the tenant, or a permission the connector requests is not listed under the app registration's **API permissions** (so **Grant admin consent** never covered it). | Confirm that every permission selected under **Access** on the Config page, plus `User.Read` and `offline_access`, is listed under the app registration's **API permissions**. Add any that are missing, then select **Grant admin consent** (step 4). |
| Entra error `AADSTS7000218` at sign-in | **Allow public client flows** is set to **No** on the app registration. | Set it to **Yes** (step 3). |
| Entra error `AADSTS53000` or `AADSTS53003` when Claude calls Microsoft 365 | A Conditional Access policy requires a compliant or managed device, and either sign-in fell back to the browser because brokered sign-in is not available, or the device does not satisfy the policy's grant control. | Meet the [brokered sign-in requirements](#brokered-sign-in-requirements) for the member's platform, confirm the device satisfies whichever grant control your policy applies (marked compliant, or hybrid joined), and restart Claude Desktop. If the error returns, have the member select **Disconnect**, then **Connect**. |
| Entra error `AADSTS700016` at sign-in | The **Client ID** or **Tenant ID** on the Config page does not match an application in the selected **Azure cloud**. | Re-check the Client ID and Tenant ID against the application's Overview page, and confirm that **Azure cloud** matches the cloud where you registered the application. |
| Sign-in or Claude's Microsoft 365 calls fail with a network error and no `AADSTS` code | The member's device cannot reach the Microsoft Entra or Microsoft Graph host for your Azure cloud. | Allow outbound HTTPS to the hosts listed under [Allow outbound network access](#allow-outbound-network-access). |
| A tool returns a permission error | The Microsoft Graph permission that tool needs is not approved on the app registration, or is not selected under **Access**. | Add the permission in both places and select **Grant admin consent** again. |
| Claude finds a OneNote file but cannot open it | Claude cannot open OneNote notebooks or read their pages. | Have the member export the pages from OneNote as a PDF and save the PDF to OneDrive or SharePoint, where Claude can read it. |


# Connectors
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/connectors/overview

Connectors let tenant administrators and organization owners add their agency's MCP servers: who gets them, authentication, OAuth redirect URIs, tool policy.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators and organization owners who want Claude to reach their agency's own systems (for example, an internal search service or a ticketing tool) from Claude Desktop and other Claude products.

Use this page to add Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for your own systems, choose which Claude products receive each one, and set which of their tools are available to members.

A **connector** is a link between Claude and an external service. The service, your agency's own or a vendor's, runs an MCP server, which is a standard way for a service to publish a set of tools that Claude can call. You add the server once here, and Claude for Government delivers it to the products you select.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These cases are covered on other pages:
>
> * **The Microsoft 365 connector**: see [Set up the Microsoft 365 connector](/docs/government/connectors/microsoft-365)
> * **Plugins**: see [Manage plugins and connectors](/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors)

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Connectors and plugins" />

Video: Connectors and plugins (2 min 8 s). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

[Transcript](/docs/government/video-walkthroughs#connectors-and-plugins)

## Who receives a connector

To see or add connectors, go to **Settings > Config** and open the **Connectors** card, under **Integrations**. A connector reaches the people whose settings you are editing when you add it: everyone in the [tenant](/docs/government/tenant-admin/configuration), everyone in an [organization](/docs/government/org-admin/configuration), or the members of one directory group, as described under [Group-specific settings](/docs/government/config/overview#group-specific-settings). In every case it is delivered only to the products you select, with the tool policy you set.

A connector added for a group does not always reach every member of the group. Only one group's settings, connectors included, apply to each person, as described under [When someone belongs to more than one group](/docs/government/config/overview#when-someone-belongs-to-more-than-one-group).

When the same connector name is added at more than one level, each member receives only the entry from the [most specific level](/docs/government/config/overview#how-settings-are-applied) that applies to them. That entry replaces the others as a whole, including its address, authentication, products, and tool policy.

### Change or stop an inherited connector

Unless a level above has [locked](/docs/government/config/overview#locks) the **Connectors** card, you can change an inherited connector for the members at your level: click **Add connector** and create one with the same name. The inherited connector's details and stored secret are not copied, so you enter the server address, authentication, and tool policy again. You cannot remove a connector inherited from a level above, but in the same way you can stop it from reaching the members at your level: add one with the same name and select no products under **Apply to**.

## Adding a connector

Go to **Settings > Config**, open the **Connectors** card, and click **Add connector**. On the tenant Config page, you first choose whether organizations **May set their own value** or **Must use this value**, which stops organizations and groups from adding connectors or replacing yours.

### Server address and authentication

* **Name** is a short identifier for the connector. It must be letters a to z in either case, digits, hyphens, or underscores. Claude Desktop shows members [the name](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#managedmcpservers) with the capital letters you type. If you add a connector with a name already used at your level, even with different capital letters, the new connector replaces that one, tool policy included.
* **Server URL** is the address of the server's MCP endpoint. It must begin with `https://`. Enter the address the server answers on, not one that redirects to it. Claude Desktop [connects to it directly from each member's device](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#connectors), so the server, and its sign-in provider if it uses OAuth, must be reachable from those devices. You do not need to ask Anthropic to allow either address.
* **Transport** selects how Claude talks to the server. Choose HTTP or SSE to match what your server supports.
* **Authentication** selects how Claude proves who it is to the server:
  * **None** is for a server that needs no sign-in: it sends no credentials. If the server asks for sign-in anyway, Claude Desktop [lets each member sign in](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/extensions#oauth-sign-in).
  * **Header (shared secret)** sends a fixed header (for example, an authorization token) with every request; the value is stored securely and shown as `••••` after you save, and each member's app receives it.
  * **OAuth (members sign in)** has each member sign in on first use, and their tokens stay on their own machine. Choose it when the server's sign-in provider lets apps register themselves (dynamic client registration).
  * **OAuth (pre-registered app)** also has each member sign in, through an app you register with the server's sign-in provider ahead of time. Choose it when the provider has you create an app and copy its client ID.

Neither OAuth option stores a secret. If the server's sign-in provider requires a client secret, members can't connect to that server.

When you choose either OAuth option, a confirmation checkbox appears on the final step asking you to confirm that the server address is exactly the one you intend, because members are sent to a sign-in page that the server chooses. When sign-in happens somewhere other than the server itself, for example when you set a tenant ID for a Microsoft Entra app, the checkbox names both that sign-in address and the server address.

### Register an app for sign-in

For **OAuth (pre-registered app)**, add Claude Desktop's [redirect URI](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/extensions#oauth-sign-in), `http://127.0.0.1:53280/callback`, to the app's registration with your sign-in provider. If the registration uses another port or `localhost`, set **Callback port** or **Callback host** in the wizard to match. Have the app's client ID ready, and for a single-tenant Microsoft Entra app its tenant ID and scope as well.

For the Claude Code command-line tool, set **Callback port** to the port you registered for Claude Desktop. Also add `http://localhost:PORT/callback`, with that port, to the registration. A connector with a tenant ID is not delivered to the command-line tool.

Enter the scope that your server's own API expects (for example, an `api://` scope for an app registered in your tenant), because Microsoft Graph scopes such as `Mail.Read` would give the connector's server access to members' Microsoft 365 data.

### Tool discovery

The wizard tries to list the tools the server offers, so that you can set policy on them. Discovery runs from your own browser and is best-effort; many servers cannot be reached this way (for example, because they require authentication or are on a private network), and you can always add tools by name on the next step instead.

Discovery can ask you to sign in to the server. The credential is used once in your browser for this probe and is never stored; it is separate from the **Authentication** choice on the Server step, which controls how members authenticate later.

### Products and tool policy

Under **Apply to**, tick the products that should receive this connector. **Microsoft 365** is the [Claude for Microsoft 365 add-in](/docs/government/deploy-microsoft-365/configure#before-you-begin), which cannot receive a connector that uses OAuth or that has any tool switched off.

Under **Tool policy**, switch each of the server's tools on or off, or leave it unlisted. On Claude Desktop, that tool policy shapes what members experience:

* A tool you switch off is blocked, so Claude cannot use it.
* A tool you switch on is available and asks the member on every use, and members are not offered a lasting approval for it. Its permission control is locked, and hovering over it shows **Permission set by your admin**.
* A tool you do not list is left to the member to turn on or off, and its approval prompts follow the member's own choices, which can include lasting approval. To return a listed tool to each member's control, remove its row.

A saved connector reaches members as described under [When changes take effect](/docs/government/config/overview#when-changes-take-effect).

### Connection to server failed

If **Connect** in Claude Desktop shows "Connection to server failed. You can try again.", check first that the device can reach the server's address, that the app you registered lists the redirect URI, and that no other program is using the callback port. When the provider doesn't list the redirect URI, its own error page opens in the member's browser. In the other two cases the member's [`main.log`](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#troubleshooting) records the reason. [How OAuth sign-in works](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/extensions#how-oauth-sign-in-works) lists other causes.

## Editing and removing a connector

To change a connector, edit it on the **Connectors** card. Changing the authentication method clears any stored secret and the app details saved for **OAuth (pre-registered app)**.

Click the remove button next to a connector to delete it; it is withdrawn from every product [when the change takes effect](/docs/government/config/overview#when-changes-take-effect). If you delete a connector that takes priority over an inherited connector with the same name, the inherited connector applies again.


# Connect Claude Code to Claude for Government
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/deploy-claude-code/configure

Connect the Claude Code command-line tool to Claude for Government with managed settings on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and confirm a device is set up.

> **Who this is for:** IT administrators who install the Claude Code command-line tool on agency devices and connect it to Claude for Government.

In Claude for Government, Claude Code is in early access. To request access for your agency, contact your Anthropic representative.

Each device needs managed settings that send users to your agency's Claude for Government sign-in. The organization's Claude Code settings are set on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings) page.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Claude Code in Claude Desktop's **Code** tab signs in through Claude Desktop and is turned on by the [**Code in Claude Desktop**](/docs/government/config/settings#code-in-claude-desktop) switch, not the **Claude Code** switch; see [Connect Claude Desktop to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure). The `env` block of these managed settings still applies to Code tab sessions. For the other settings that govern them on a device that also has these managed settings, see [Code in Claude Desktop](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#code-in-claude-desktop).

## Before you begin

* **Claude Code is turned on for the organization.** A tenant administrator or organization owner turns on the **Claude Code** switch under [Product availability](/docs/government/config/settings#product-availability) on the **Config** page. It is off by default, and while it is off, Claude Code exits right after the user signs in.
* **User accounts exist.** Claude Code signs users in to the same accounts as this portal. Each user needs a [routing rule](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access) that covers them and a [seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) with at least one model enabled.
* **Claude Code is current.** This setup requires Claude Code 2.1.274 or later (`claude --version` in a terminal).
* **Devices can reach Claude for Government.** Claude Code must reach the gateway address over HTTPS on port 443, and the user's browser must reach the same sign-in hosts that [Claude Desktop needs](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#network-access).
* **You can place a system-level file or policy.** The settings are enforced only from a system file, a macOS configuration profile, or a machine-level Windows policy, and values for the same keys in a user's own settings cannot override them.

## The managed settings

For Claude for Government, Claude Code's [managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings) contain these keys, shown as a `managed-settings.json` file:

```json theme={null}
{
  "forceLoginMethod": "gateway",
  "forceLoginGatewayUrl": "https://<claude-for-government-host>/gateway-api",
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC": "1",
    "DISABLE_TELEMETRY": "1",
    "DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING": "1",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL": "1",
    "ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS": "",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY": "",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_METADATA": "",
    "NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED": "1",
    "NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS": ""
  },
  "parentSettingsBehavior": "merge"
}
```

* **`forceLoginMethod`** (required): replaces Claude Code's sign-in choices with a single **Cloud gateway** screen.
* **`forceLoginGatewayUrl`** (required): the Claude for Government gateway address that the **Cloud gateway** screen connects to. If your agency reaches Claude for Government on a hostname of its own, ask your Anthropic representative which address to use. Otherwise, replace `<claude-for-government-host>` with the domain name you use to access Claude for Government, the host in your Claude Desktop [`bootstrapUrl`](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#the-managed-setting). The address contains no credentials.
* **`env`** (required): holds the variables that [Before sign-in](#before-sign-in) describes.
* **`parentSettingsBehavior`** (devices that also run Claude Desktop): where these managed settings govern Claude Desktop's sessions, `"merge"` layers the policy that Claude Desktop supplies, Code's sandbox included, under them. Without it, Claude Code [can ignore that policy](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/code#interaction-with-claude-code%E2%80%99s-own-managed-settings).

### Before sign-in

Your organization's settings reach Claude Code only after a user has signed in. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL` together keep Claude Code's release-notes download, update checks, automatic setup of the official plugin marketplace, and usage telemetry and error reporting to Anthropic off from the first launch. They stay off after sign-in.

Every variable in the sample is required. `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_METADATA` must be empty strings, so a user's or a repository's settings file can't change them. `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` must be `"1"`, which keeps certificate checking on. `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is the path to your agency's certificate authority bundle if your devices need one, as [TLS inspection can require](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config#ca-certificate-store), and is otherwise empty.

For Claude Code's other environment variables, see [Environment variables](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) in the Claude Code documentation.

### Web proxy settings

If your devices use a web proxy that you manage, add `HTTPS_PROXY` and `HTTP_PROXY` (the proxy's address, for example `http://proxy.example.corp:8080`) and `NO_PROXY` (your bypass list, keeping `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `::1`) to the same `env` block, each under both its uppercase and lowercase name. Claude Code then uses that proxy wherever the device connects from, in place of any other proxy setting on the device. Signing in through a proxy whose address starts with `https://` requires Claude Code 2.1.307 or later. If your devices connect directly, leave these variables out rather than setting them to empty strings, because an empty value switches off a proxy a user would otherwise use.

## Deploy the settings

Deliver the settings through your device management system wherever you can, and before users start Claude Code for the first time, so that their first launch opens the **Cloud gateway** screen. Use one location for each device. Claude Desktop runs Chat, Cowork, and Code through its own Claude Code, which reads these settings, including [proxy values](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/network-proxy#interaction-with-claude-code-managed-settings) and any [`requiredMaximumVersion`](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#claude-code-maximum-version). For how they combine with your organization's settings, see [Code in Claude Desktop](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#code-in-claude-desktop).

### macOS

Place the managed settings file at `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json`, or deploy a configuration profile that sets the same top-level keys in the `com.anthropic.claudecode` managed preferences domain, with `env` as a dictionary of strings.

### Windows

Place the managed settings file at `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json`, or deliver it as machine policy: a `REG_SZ` value named `Settings` under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode` holding the whole JSON document, as in this `.reg` file:

```text theme={null}
Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode]
; substitute your gateway address from "The managed settings"
"Settings"="{\"forceLoginMethod\":\"gateway\",\"forceLoginGatewayUrl\":\"https://<claude-for-government-host>/gateway-api\",\"env\":{\"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC\":\"1\",\"DISABLE_TELEMETRY\":\"1\",\"DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING\":\"1\",\"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL\":\"1\",\"ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS\":\"\",\"CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY\":\"\",\"CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_METADATA\":\"\",\"NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED\":\"1\",\"NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS\":\"\"},\"parentSettingsBehavior\":\"merge\"}"
```

A value under `HKEY_CURRENT_USER` does not turn on gateway sign-in.

### Linux and Windows Subsystem for Linux

On Linux, place the managed settings file at `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` (root required).

Claude Code inside Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) reads that same path inside each distribution. To manage the settings from Windows instead, add `"wslInheritsWindowsSettings": true` to the machine-level Windows policy or file alongside the other keys. Claude Code inside WSL then reads the Windows settings first and needs no file inside the distribution.

## Sign in

Before a user's first gateway sign-in, have them remove any earlier claude.ai sign-in with `claude auth logout` in a terminal, or VS Code's **Claude Code: Logout** command. Signing out later also removes the gateway sign-in. VS Code extension users who sign in through the gateway in a terminal need the standalone command-line tool. The copy of Claude Code that the extension runs follows these managed settings and must also meet the [minimum version](#before-you-begin). The version of the copy it bundles is the extension's version number in VS Code's **Extensions** view.
