>
> If you can sign in but the model picker is empty, ask your organization's owner to check your seat tier and its models.

* **Claude Desktop is up to date.** Update Claude Desktop to 4.29.0 or later and restart it, or ask your IT administrator to update it.
* **You had an account on the web app.** Its work email address must match the one on your account in Claude Desktop.

> **For administrators:** Anthropic enables the import for each organization. If a member's **Import & export** page says import is not enabled and their app is up to date, contact your Anthropic representative. The import needs Claude Desktop to download a component, so on a network that blocks `downloads.claude.ai`, deploy the offline installer described under [Installer and packaging](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/windows-checklist#installer-and-packaging) in the Windows fleet checklist.

## Run the import

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Bringing your chats and projects over from Claude for Government Web" />

Video: Bringing your chats and projects over from Claude for Government Web (2 min 9 s). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

> [accordion] Transcript
>
> If you used Claude for Government Web, you can copy your chats and projects into Claude Desktop. First, make sure Claude Desktop is up to date. You need an account on the web app, and it must use the same work email as your account in Claude Desktop.
>
> In Claude Desktop, open Settings from the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar, then Import and export, and select Import. Run it when you are ready.
>
> Select Sign in to Claude for Government Web, then Sign in. Claude shows a one-time code and opens a tab in your browser.
>
> In that tab, enter the code from Claude and approve the request. If you are asked to sign in, use your work account. Then go back to Claude.
>
> Check that the email shown is yours, then select Fetch export, and wait while Claude downloads your chats and projects.
>
> Select Continue, review what will be added, then select Import. When it finishes, the dialog reports what came over. Select Done.
>
> Your conversations appear in the sidebar, and your projects under Projects. Projects other people shared with you do not come over.
>
> Imported chats open in Chat. The first time you continue one, Claude asks whether to resume the imported session. Select Trust and resume to continue the conversation.
>
> A project that had instructions shows a notice. Claude won't follow imported instructions until you accept them: select Review instructions, check them, and save, or choose Use as is.
>
> The import only copies. You can run it again, and chats already imported are skipped. If the Import and export page says import isn't enabled, update Claude Desktop. If it still says so, ask your administrator.

You start the import yourself from **Settings**, whenever you are ready. If Claude Desktop's home screen shows a **Pick up where you left off in Claude for Government Web** banner, its **Start import** button takes you to the **Import & export** page in **Settings**. If you click **Skip for now** or close the banner, it can come back a few days later, until you run the import or have skipped it a few times. Claude Desktop versions earlier than 2.16120.0 hide the banner permanently after one skip.

**1. Open the import dialog**

In Claude Desktop, open **Settings**, then the **Import & export** page, and click **Import…**.

**2. Sign in and enter the code**

Click **Sign in to Claude for Government Web…**, and in the dialog that opens, click **Sign in**. Claude Desktop shows a one-time code, which expires after a few minutes, and opens a tab in your default browser. In that tab, enter the code and approve the request. If you are asked to sign in, use your work account. Then return to Claude Desktop.

**3. Fetch your export**

Check that the email address shown is your work address, then click **Fetch export** and wait for the download to finish.

**4. Start the import**

Click **Continue**, review what will be added, then click **Import**. The import can take a few minutes.

**5. Check the results**

When the dialog reports what it brought over, click **Done**. Imported conversations appear in the sidebar, and imported projects appear under **Projects**.

## Continue an imported conversation

The first time you send a message in an imported conversation, Claude Desktop shows a **Resume imported session?** prompt. Click **Trust and resume** to continue.

## Review imported project instructions

If a project had instructions in the web app, open it after the import. Its page shows a notice that the instructions came from an import, and Claude does not follow them until you accept them. Click **Review instructions** to edit and save them, or **Use as is** to accept them unchanged. They then appear under **Instructions** on the project's page. Claude Desktop versions earlier than 1.25927.0 follow imported instructions straight away.

## Remove an import

To remove an import, open **Settings**, then the **Import & export** page. Under **Import history**, click **Remove** next to the import, or **Remove all** to remove every import listed. Before you confirm, the dialog shows how many conversations and projects it will delete. The files of imported projects stay on your computer, by default in `Claude/Projects` in your home folder, until you delete them yourself.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Removing an import also deletes any imported conversation you have continued since, including the new messages, and you cannot undo it.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | Likely cause | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| Your export exceeds the import size limit | You have more data than the import can bring over | Update Claude Desktop to 4.29.0 or later, then run the import again. If you still see this message, contact your administrator, who can ask Anthropic for help |
| The account does not match your organization | You signed in with a different account or organization | Click **Sign in** in the dialog again and use your work account in the browser tab |
| **Settings** has no **Import & export** page, or the page says import isn't enabled for this deployment | Your app is out of date, or Anthropic has not yet enabled the import for your organization | Update Claude Desktop to the latest version. If the page still says import isn't enabled, contact your administrator, who can ask Anthropic to enable it |

For anything else, try the import again; if it keeps failing, contact your administrator.

## Things to know

* **You can run the import again.** Conversations you already imported are skipped.
* **Conversations can arrive as Cowork tasks.** If your organization's [settings](/docs/government/config/settings#product-availability) do not give you Chat when you run the import, your conversations are imported as Cowork tasks instead and open only on computers where Cowork is available. Claude Desktop versions earlier than 1.28929.0 always import them as Cowork tasks.
* **Projects other people shared with you are not imported.** Only the projects you created come over.
* **When Claude Desktop is connected to Claude for Government, it does not offer an import from claude.ai.**
* **In Chat, Claude can't read a folder that the import put on a project until you add the folder to the project again.** For the steps, see [Make an imported project folder readable in Chat](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/import#make-an-imported-project-folder-readable-in-chat).


# Models in Claude Desktop
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/desktop/models

Switch models in Claude Desktop on Claude for Government, see what the 1M context window does, and find what controls which models you see.

> **Who this is for:** Anyone who uses Claude Desktop in Claude for Government. The last section is for administrators.

The model picker shows which Claude model answers you and lets you switch to another. Which models it lists depends on the [seat tier](/docs/government/account/profile) your organization has assigned to you, so a colleague may see a different list.

A model that needs a newer version of Claude Desktop does not appear in the picker until the app is updated. If you are missing a model that a colleague on the same seat tier has, update Claude Desktop, or ask your IT administrator to update it.

## Larger context window

The context window is how much of a conversation Claude can keep in view at once, measured in tokens (a token is a short piece of text, roughly a word or part of one). Some models offer a window of about one million tokens (1M). Such a model appears once in the picker, and new conversations, tasks, and Code sessions on it use the 1M window.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Before Claude Desktop 2.31226.0, such a model appears twice. To be sure of the larger window, check that the entry marked **1M context window**, or **1M** in Code, is selected when you start new work.

When a long conversation or task gets close to filling the context window, Claude summarizes the earlier part to make room and carries on from the summary, which the app calls compacting. With a 1M window this happens much later than with a window of about 200,000 tokens (200K). Past the point where a 200K window would compact, each further message carries the whole conversation rather than a summary, so it uses more of your [allowance](/docs/government/account/usage) and responses can take longer to start.

## Model availability for administrators

The models a member sees come from the **Allowed models** of their [seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers). Whether a model offers the [1M context window](#larger-context-window) is set by Anthropic for each model rather than in the admin portal. When you change a tier's allowed models, access changes straight away, and the member's model picker shows the change the next time they start Claude Desktop.


# Plugins in Claude Desktop
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/desktop/plugins

Find, install, create, and remove plugins in Claude Desktop for Claude for Government, and understand what plugins add in this deployment.

> **Who this is for:** Anyone who uses Claude Desktop in Claude for Government and wants to find, install, or create plugins.

A plugin is a package that adds capabilities to Claude in a single step, such as skills, slash commands, sub-agents, and hooks. Plugins work in Cowork and in Code. Skills from your organization's plugins also work in Chat, on Claude Desktop 1.44121.4 or later. [What a Chat conversation can reach](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/chat#what-a-chat-conversation-can-reach) says what else a plugin adds there.

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Connectors, plugins, and skills from your agency" />

Video: Connectors, plugins, and skills from your agency (2 min). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

[Transcript](/docs/government/desktop/video-walkthroughs#connectors-plugins-and-skills-from-your-agency)

## Find and install plugins

Claude for Government does not include a public plugin marketplace; your administrators add your organization's plugins. Go to **Customize > Plugins** to see the plugins you have installed. To find the rest, select **Discover** (**Browse** on Claude Desktop versions earlier than 2.2553.0) and open the **Organization** tab, which lists every plugin your administrators have made available to you.

A plugin your administrators set to install automatically is already installed. A plugin they offer for you to choose stays available until you install it. If a plugin you expect is missing, ask your organization's owner.

If your administrators let you add your own plugins, **Add** on the same page lets you install a plugin from its `.zip` file or have Claude build one. If those options are missing, your administrators haven't allowed them. A plugin you upload or create is added only on the device you are using. Claude Desktop shows a notice reminding you to install only plugins you trust, since uploaded plugins are not controlled by Anthropic.

If your administrators let you add plugin marketplaces, you can add a marketplace of your own from **Discover**. Whether a marketplace you add can be downloaded depends on your agency's network and on the settings your administrators choose.

## Manage installed plugins

Go to **Customize > Plugins** and open an installed plugin to see what it provides, turn it on or off, or remove it. Plugins you remove stay removed on this device, including ones your administrators set to install automatically.

## What plugins add in Claude for Government

A plugin's hooks run on your machine at defined points during a session. The connectors your administrators provide appear under **Customize > Connectors**. A plugin can also declare connectors of its own. Whether they connect depends on the settings your administrators choose.


# Skills in Claude Desktop
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/desktop/skills

Skills in Claude Desktop for Claude for Government: where they come from, how to create and manage your own, and how administrators distribute them.

> **Who this is for:** Anyone who uses Claude Desktop in Claude for Government. The last section is for administrators who distribute skills to members.

A skill is a set of instructions, with optional scripts and resources, that Claude loads when a task matches it, so you can teach Claude a workflow once and reuse it.

## Where skills come from

In Claude for Government, your skills come from these places:

* Skills you create yourself.
* Skills bundled in plugins your administrators deliver, which arrive with the plugin as described in [Plugins in Claude Desktop](/docs/government/desktop/plugins).
* Skills that ship with Claude Desktop for common document tasks, such as working with spreadsheets and presentations, which Claude loads automatically when a task calls for them.

## Create and manage skills

Go to **Customize > Skills** to see your skills and turn them on or off. If your administrators let you create skills, **Add** on that page lets you write one or upload a skill file you have, and you can ask Claude to save a workflow as a skill while you work on a task. If those options are missing, your administrators haven't allowed them. The [skill authoring guide](/docs/skills/how-to) describes the file format for skills you write yourself.

Open a skill you created to delete it. Skills you create are stored on your device, so they are available only there.

## Skills for administrators

The admin portal does not have a skills view or per-skill controls, so there is no setting that allows, blocks, or distributes a skill on its own. [**Let members create skills**](/docs/government/config/settings#let-members-create-skills) controls whether members can create or upload skills of their own.

To distribute skills to the members you manage, bundle them in a plugin, as described under [Package a skill as a plugin](/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors#package-a-skill-as-a-plugin). A skill you distribute this way is managed through the plugin that carries it, so to change or retire the skill, [update or remove the plugin](/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors#update-or-remove-a-plugin).
