# Moving from Claude for Government Web
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/moving-from-web

Find answers to the questions agencies ask most often when moving from Claude for Government Web to Claude Desktop.

> **Who this is for:** Administrators and IT staff at an agency that used Claude for Government Web (the web app) and is moving its users to Claude Desktop connected to Claude for Government. If you use Claude but don't administer it, see [Import your data from Claude for Government Web](/docs/government/desktop/import) instead.

This page answers the questions that only come up during the move and links each one to the page with the detail. For anything specific to your agency's agreement, contact your Anthropic representative.

## What the move involves

* **Can users still open the web app?** No, Claude for Government Web is retired. Users can still [run the import](/docs/government/desktop/import).
* **Do users need the Claude Desktop app?** Yes. After the move, people use Claude in the Claude Desktop app (Chat, Cowork, and Code), which your IT team deploys, and use the browser only to sign in, view [their account](/docs/government/account/overview), and administer. See [Connect Claude Desktop to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure).
* **What changes for users?** They work in the Claude Desktop app instead of a browser, and conversations, projects, and files are stored on each user's device, so projects aren't shared between people. Administrators can still give everyone in the tenant or in one organization the same skills by adding them as a plugin in the admin portal. See [Data storage and retention](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#data-storage-and-retention), [Chat and Cowork differences](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#chat-and-cowork-differences), and [Skills for administrators](/docs/government/desktop/skills#skills-for-administrators).
* **Does anything carry over from the web app?** Each user can copy their own conversations and projects with the [Claude for Government Web import](/docs/government/desktop/import). Roles and administrative settings aren't copied from the web app, so your administrators set up the admin portal themselves, starting with the [setup wizard](/docs/government/tenant-admin/setup-wizard).
* **Do Compliance API keys carry over from the web app?** No. Create a new key in the admin portal and point your SIEM or log tool at the new address. A tool left on the old address misses new events and may show no error. Event types and request parameters also differ from the web app's. See [Compliance API](/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api).
* **Can the web app's application be deleted from your identity provider?** Check the **Single sign-on** card on [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#single-sign-on) first. If the card's **Redirect URI / ACS URL** appears in that application, Claude for Government signs people in through it. If the application is deleted, single sign-on stops for everyone, and removing users from it can stop theirs.
* **What does each user do?** Install or receive Claude Desktop, choose **Sign in with your organization**, and optionally [run the import](/docs/government/desktop/import).

## First sign-ins and the admin portal

* **Where is the admin portal?** In the browser, at your Claude for Government address followed by `/gateway`, not in the Claude Desktop app. See [The three views](/docs/government/overview#the-three-views) for which view each role opens.
* **How does the first administrator sign in, before single sign-on is connected?** On the sign-in page at your Claude for Government address followed by `/gateway`, which can email them a single-use sign-in link. See [Tenant setup wizard](/docs/government/tenant-admin/setup-wizard).
* **How are user accounts created?** At each person's first sign-in through a routing rule, or ahead of time through SCIM. See [Routing rules](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#routing-rules) and [How seats are assigned automatically](/docs/government/org-admin/seats#how-seats-are-assigned-automatically).
* **Single sign-on works, but users are told they haven't been added to an organization.** A routing rule must cover them. See [Routing rules](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#routing-rules) and the [Readiness](/docs/government/tenant-admin/readiness) page.

## Deployment and network

* **Is this a separate government app?** No, it's the same Claude Desktop app used everywhere. Managed settings that your IT team deploys connect it to Claude for Government, and until a device has them, the app shows the regular claude.ai sign-in. See [Deploy to your fleet](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#deploy-to-your-fleet) and [Order of deployment](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#order-of-deployment).
* **Which hosts must the firewall allow, and what if claude.ai is blocked?** See [Network egress, required domains, and proxies](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#network-egress-required-domains-and-proxies) and [Network access](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#network-access).
* **Can Chat be rolled out first and Cowork enabled later?** Yes. See [If some devices are not ready for Cowork](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/windows-checklist#if-some-devices-are-not-ready-for-cowork).

## The Claude for Government Web import

* **How do users bring over their conversations and projects?** Each user runs the import themselves, once their Claude Desktop is [up to date](/docs/government/desktop/import#before-you-begin). See [Import your data from Claude for Government Web](/docs/government/desktop/import).
* **Can administrators remind users to run the import?** Yes. Turn on the [**Show the Claude for Government Web import banner**](/docs/government/config/settings#show-the-claude-for-government-web-import-banner) switch on the **Config** page.
* **The Import & export page in Claude Desktop says import isn't enabled.** See [Troubleshooting](/docs/government/desktop/import#troubleshooting) on the import page.
* **What comes across, and how does a user redo an import?** See [Things to know](/docs/government/desktop/import#things-to-know) and [Remove an import](/docs/government/desktop/import#remove-an-import).

## Other questions

Everything that isn't specific to the move, such as single sign-on, SCIM, seats, usage limits, settings, and connectors, is in the [Claude for Government administrator guide](/docs/government/overview) and the pages listed beside it. Security and compliance reviewers start at [Security and data handling](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling). To report a problem, administrators contact their Anthropic representative or use the **Support** link in the admin portal footer, and service status is on [status.claude.com](https://status.claude.com) under Claude for Government.


# Analytics
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/analytics

Review your organization's requests, tokens, spend, active users, top users, and credit balance over time, and download the data as CSV files for reporting.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners who need to understand how their organization is using Claude and how quickly it is consuming credits.

The **Analytics** page shows requests, tokens, spend, top users, and credit balance over time across your organization. Usage figures on this page are compiled from the same metering that enforces your users' spend limits. All times are shown in your browser's time zone.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These cases are covered on other pages:
>
> * **How close each user is to their 5-hour and 7-day limits**: use the **Usage** bars on the [Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users#reset-usage-limits) page
> * **Usage records sent to your own collector**: see [Compliance and telemetry](/docs/government/config/settings#compliance-and-telemetry)

## Managed and self-managed views

**Anthropic-managed tiers** and **Self-managed tiers** are shown separately because their economics differ: managed-tier seats are purchased as seats, while self-managed tiers (tiers your organization created itself on the [Tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) page) draw down the billing account's balance. Spend figures and the credit panel are shown only in the **Self-managed** view. If your organization has only one kind of tier, the page shows only the matching view.

## Credits (self-managed view only)

When credit data is available, the credit panel displays the **Credits remaining** for the account your organization draws from. It also shows a runway estimate that tells you roughly how many days remain at your organization's own trailing 7-day burn rate. A **Low balance** badge appears as the balance runs low, and a **Depleted** badge replaces it when no credits remain.

The **Credit burndown** chart plots your balance, with markers on the days credits were added, and projects forward at that rate to the date you are estimated to reach \$0.

## Active users

The **Active users** section shows how many distinct people used Claude over fixed periods, as daily, weekly, and monthly active users. A user counts as **active** if Claude answered them at least once in the period.

## Usage

Everything below the **Usage** divider is scoped to a time window that you choose, from **24 hours** to **90 days**. The figures are requests, input tokens, output tokens, and, in the self-managed view, estimated spend. Estimated spend includes input stored or reused through prompt caching. Input tokens do not, so token counts alone understate cost.

* The **By product** table breaks usage down by which Claude product it came from (for example, Claude Desktop or Claude Code). Chat and Cowork activity in Claude Desktop is counted together in a single Claude Desktop row. Code sessions in Claude Desktop run on Claude Code, so they are counted in the Claude Code row along with any use of the standalone Claude Code command-line tool.
* The **By model** table lists each model used in the window.
* The **Top users** table lists the users with the most tokens in the window, and each user's figures combine their usage across all products. Up to 100 users are listed individually, and beyond that a note tells you how many more are not listed. Usage from before a person's move stays with the organization they left.

## CSV exports

The **Download** menu saves what the page shows as CSV files. **All** downloads a ZIP archive of the current view, one CSV file per table. The other entries download one table each.

* **What an export covers.** Exports follow the view and the time window you have selected. The credit files match the burndown chart, reaching back 30 days, or 90 days when you select the **90 days** window. In the summary file, the credit figures are the account's position at the time of the export, not spend within the window.
* **Export context.** The ZIP archive includes an `export_info.csv` file recording the export's context, including when it was made, the organization, the view, the window and its date range, and the time zone the dates are in.
* **Per-user data.** The top users file lists the same users as the **Top users** table, up to 100, and adds each user's ID and account status to the columns shown on screen.

Claude for Government does not offer a programmatic usage or analytics API. Usage data is available through this admin portal page. The [Compliance API](/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api) returns governance and audit events, not usage metrics.


# Billing
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/billing

See the balance your organization spends from, the spend caps set on it, and its seats, and what happens as the billing account's balance runs low.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners who want to see the balance their organization spends from, any spend caps set on it, and its seat allocation.

A **billing account** is the funding pool that pays for one or more organizations in your tenant. Your organization's usage on [self-managed seat tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#anthropic-managed-versus-self-managed-tiers) draws directly from this account's balance, and Anthropic adds credit to the account.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The **Billing** tab appears in the navigation when the billing account is active and your own organization is active on it. Funding is arranged with Anthropic by your tenant administrators; contact them about credits or spend caps.

## Billing account

The page shows the account's available balance if your organization uses self-managed seat tiers and either manages the account or is the only organization on it. Otherwise it says why no balance is shown. The balance is shared by every organization the account funds. Your organization's usage against the account balance is shown on the [Analytics](/docs/government/org-admin/analytics) page.

The page also shows the [spend caps](/docs/government/tenant-admin/credits#how-billing-works) currently set on your organization. These caps are set by your tenant administrator and cannot be changed here. A cap of \$0 pauses your organization's spending from the account.

As the account's balance runs low, and again when it runs out and requests are refused, a spend-alert banner appears on every page of the organization admin portal and an email is sent to your organization's Owners and Primary Owners. The banner stays in place until Anthropic adds more credits to the account. People on Anthropic-managed seat tiers keep working, so [moving someone to one](/docs/government/org-admin/users#assigning-a-seat-tier) gets them working again. An organization that has only Anthropic-managed seat tiers gets neither banner nor email, so moving everyone to them and [deleting your self-managed tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#deleting-a-tier) also clears the banner.

## Seats

The **Seats** section shows the seats allocated to your organization. Whoever manages the billing account can change them:

* **Your tenant administrators manage the account.** Ask a tenant administrator.
* **Your organization manages the account.** A Primary Owner sees the account's seat pool here. Enter the number you want for each tier and click **Save**. The change takes effect immediately.

If a save is refused, see [Change seat allocations](/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats#change-seat-allocations). For who is seated when seats are added, see [How seats are assigned automatically](/docs/government/org-admin/seats#how-seats-are-assigned-automatically).


# Compliance API
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api

Stream your organization's audit events into a SIEM or log management system.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners, tenant administrators, and the security or compliance teams who connect Claude for Government to their agency's log management or SIEM platform.

The Compliance API is a read-only HTTP endpoint that lets your security tools pull a continuous feed of audit events covering administrative activity across your organization, such as sign-ins, role changes, key creations, and seat assignments. A scheduled job can poll the endpoint and forward each event to a SIEM such as Splunk or Microsoft Sentinel.

The API is available to every Claude for Government organization by default, and it is read-only, so a compromised key cannot change anything in your organization.

## Managing API keys

To create and manage keys for your organization, open **Compliance API** under **Settings** in the [organization admin portal](/docs/government/org-admin/overview#who-can-access-it). To create and manage keys that return events for every organization in your tenant, open **Compliance API keys** under **Settings** in the [tenant admin portal](/docs/government/tenant-admin/overview). Only tenant administrators can open the tenant admin portal.

Both pages list only their own keys, showing each key's name, a hint with the last few characters of the key so you can tell keys apart, when the key was created, and whether it is active or revoked.

To create a key, enter a name and click **Create key**. The full value is shown once, immediately after creation. Copy it somewhere safe before clicking **Done**.

> [!WARNING]
>
> The full key value is shown **only once**, at creation time. If you lose it, create a new key and revoke the old one.

Keys never expire on their own, so rotate them on whatever schedule your agency's policy requires. You can keep more than one key active at a time, which lets you rotate without interrupting your SIEM feed: create a new key, update your collector to use it, confirm events are still arriving, and then revoke the old key. Revoking a key takes effect immediately, and the next request made with it returns a 401.

Each key is scoped to the organization or tenant it was created in. A key created in the organization admin portal returns events for that one organization only, regardless of who holds the key. A key that a tenant administrator creates in the tenant admin portal returns the events of every organization in the tenant, together with tenant-level activity such as changes to single sign-on, to the list of tenant administrators, and to tenant-wide settings.

## Calling the API

Send a GET request to your Claude for Government host followed by the fixed path `/gateway-api/v1/compliance/activities`, with your key in the `x-api-key` header. The Claude for Government host is the domain name in the address of your organization admin portal. If you are unsure of it, ask your Anthropic representative.

```http theme={null}
GET https://<claude-for-government-host>/gateway-api/v1/compliance/activities?since=<start-time>&limit=500
x-api-key: <your-compliance-api-key>
```

### Query parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| - | - |
| `since` or `created_at.gte` | The earliest event time to return, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or epoch seconds. A lower bound is required on every request that does not carry a cursor. |
| `until` or `created_at.lte` | The latest event time to return, in the same format. Optional. |
| `after_id` | An opaque cursor that continues from where a previous page left off. Pass the `last_id` value from the previous response. |
| `before_id` | An opaque cursor that pages in the other direction. Pass the `first_id` value from the previous response. Cannot be combined with `after_id`. |
| `actor_ids[]` | Return only events performed by the listed actors. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one. |
| `activity_types[]` | Return only events of the listed types. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one. |
| `limit` | Maximum events per page, from 1 to 5000. Defaults to 100. |

The exclusive bounds `created_at.gt` and `created_at.lt` are also accepted if your collector needs them.

The API serves the most recent 30 days of activity. A lower bound earlier than that is treated as 30 days ago.

### Response format

The response is a JSON envelope containing a page of events and the cursors for the next and previous pages.

```json theme={null}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "activity_01js0example000000000000",
      "type": "user.signed_in",
      "created_at": "2026-07-01T14:22:09.412Z",
      "organization_id": "org_00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
      "organization_uuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
      "actor": {
        "type": "user_actor",
        "user_id": "usr_00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        "email_address": "person@agency.example.com"
      },
      "user_id": "usr_00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
      "user_email": "person@agency.example.com"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "first_id": "<opaque cursor>",
  "last_id": "<opaque cursor>"
}
```

The `actor` object identifies who performed the action. Its `type` is one of:

* `user_actor` for a person acting through the product or admin portal.
* `anthropic_actor` for an action performed by Anthropic personnel or systems on your behalf, such as initial provisioning. No individual identity is included.

Each event also carries fields specific to its type, such as the role a user was changed to or the name of a key that was created.

### Identifying users

When one of your own users performs an action, `actor.user_id` and `actor.email_address` name them, including on sign-in events. Actions taken by Anthropic personnel or automated systems appear as `anthropic_actor` with no individual identity, by design.

On every `user.*` activity, two top-level fields identify the user the event is about, so your SIEM can map events back to people in your directory without a separate lookup.

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| `user_id` | The Claude for Government user ID, in the same `usr_` format as `actor.user_id`. |
| `user_email` | The user's email address at the time of the event. |

The user an event is about is not always the actor. When an owner changes someone's role, the `actor` block names the owner and these fields name the user whose role changed. When a tenant administrator who isn't one of the organization's Primary Owners grants or removes the Primary Owner role, the `user.role_changed` event also carries a `by_tenant_admin` field set to `true`.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "activity_01js1example000000000000",
  "type": "user.role_changed",
  "created_at": "2026-07-02T09:18:33.205Z",
  "organization_id": "org_00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
  "organization_uuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
  "actor": {
    "type": "user_actor",
    "user_id": "usr_00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
    "email_address": "owner@agency.example.com"
  },
  "user_id": "usr_00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
  "user_email": "person@agency.example.com",
  "old": "user",
  "new": "owner"
}
```

### Activity types

Event types use a dotted `resource.action` naming convention. The categories emitted today include:

* **Users** such as `user.created`, `user.signed_in`, `user.role_changed`, `user.deactivated`, and `user.reactivated`.
* **Organizations** such as `org.created`, `org.renamed`, and `org.deactivated`.
* **Credentials** such as `api_key.created` and `api_key.revoked`.
* **Seats and tiers** such as `seat_allocation.set`, `seat_allocation.tier_assigned`, `seat_tier.created`, and `seat_tier.updated`.
* **Configuration** such as `org_config.capabilities_set`.
* **Tenant** such as `tenant.sso_configured`, `tenant.admin_added`, and `tenant.config_set`. Only keys created in the tenant admin portal return these types.

New types may be added over time, so a collector should forward unfamiliar types rather than reject them.

## Connecting to your SIEM

Most deployments run a small scheduled worker that polls the API on a fixed interval, forwards each event to the SIEM's HTTP ingest endpoint, and records a time watermark so the next run picks up where the last one left off. A worker that falls more than 30 days behind cannot recover the gap.

A typical run requests `since=<watermark>`, forwards every event returned, and if `has_more` is true, follows `after_id=<last_id>` for each further page until `has_more` is false. After all pages are drained, advance your watermark to one hour before the newest `created_at` you saw, because an event can reach the feed after a newer one. Event `id` values are stable and unique, so your collector should deduplicate on `id`, and can then safely retry a page or use an overlapping `since` without creating duplicate records in the SIEM.

## When the API is disabled

Your tenant administrator can turn off the **Compliance API** setting on the [tenant Config page](/docs/government/tenant-admin/configuration). When that setting is off, the **Create key** button is hidden in the organization and tenant admin portals, and every call to `/gateway-api/v1/compliance/activities` returns a 400 error, including calls made with keys that were valid before the setting changed.

Listing and revoking existing keys in either portal remains available even when the setting is off, so an exposed key can still be revoked.

## Things to know

* The Claude for Government Compliance API is served from the Claude for Government service hostname, not from `api.anthropic.com`. Use the same host you use to reach the admin portal.
* There is no separate Splunk add-on. The polling pattern described under [Connecting to your SIEM](#connecting-to-your-siem) is the reference implementation for a Splunk HTTP Event Collector job.
* The OpenTelemetry export from the Claude applications is a separate log stream, configured with **Telemetry endpoint** on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#telemetry-endpoint) page. It carries per-session tool and telemetry events to a collector you specify, while this API carries administrative audit events.
* The Compliance API returns governance and audit events only. It does not return conversation content, files, or anything your users type into Claude.
* Each organization can hold up to 50 active keys at once, and keys created in the tenant admin portal have a separate limit of 50 active keys. Revoked keys do not count toward either limit.
* Events are returned newest first within each page.
* `first_id` and `last_id` are opaque cursors. Pass them back exactly as received rather than constructing them yourself.
* If your network enforces a [tenant restriction](/docs/government/tenant-admin/tenant-restrictions), the same restriction applies to Compliance API requests.


# Config at the organization level
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/configuration

Set product settings for everyone in your organization on the Config page, and see how connectors and plugins inherited from your tenant behave there.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners who set product behavior for everyone in their organization.

In the organization view of the admin portal, go to **Settings > Config**. The Config page works the same way at the tenant and organization levels, with the same list of settings. See [How Config works](/docs/government/config/overview) for how levels, locks, and groups combine, and [Available settings](/docs/government/config/settings) for what each setting does.

A setting marked **Locked by your tenant** can be changed only by a tenant administrator; see [Locks](/docs/government/config/overview#locks). Connectors and plugins the tenant has added are labeled **Inherited from your tenant** and cannot be changed from here. A connector or plugin you add with the same name takes priority over the inherited one for your members. See [Change or stop an inherited connector](/docs/government/connectors/overview#change-or-stop-an-inherited-connector) and [Where plugins are added](/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors#where-plugins-are-added).


# Organization administration
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/overview

Manage the people, seats, and settings for a single organization within your agency: users, roles, seat tiers, usage, billing, and Config.

> **Who this portal is for:** Organization owners. If you manage multiple organizations across your agency, see the [Tenant administration](/docs/government/tenant-admin/overview) guide instead.

The organization admin portal is where you manage the people, seats, and settings for a single organization in Claude for Government.

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Organization owners: users, seat tiers, and Readiness" />

Video: Organization owners: users, seat tiers, and Readiness (1 min 48 s). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

[Transcript](/docs/government/video-walkthroughs#users-seat-tiers-and-readiness-for-organization-owners)

## Key concepts

In an organization, a member's [role](/docs/government/org-admin/users#understanding-roles) decides what they can manage, and their [seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) decides which models they can use and how much. For how organizations fit into your agency's tenant, see [How your deployment is organized](/docs/government/overview#how-your-deployment-is-organized).

## Who can access it

You can reach the organization admin portal if your role in the organization is **Owner** or **Primary Owner**. Users who hold the standard **User** role are redirected to their personal account page instead.

> **For tenant administrators:** You can also open this portal for any organization in your tenant. When the tenant has more than one organization, an organization switcher appears at the top of the admin view so you can choose which one you're managing. All the changes you make while acting as an organization apply to that organization, and the audit trail records your own identity as the actor.

## Getting around

You can reach the [user view](/docs/government/account/overview) from the **Switch to user view** link in the page footer. If you are also a tenant administrator, the footer additionally offers **Switch to tenant view**.

## Pages in this portal

* **[Setup wizard](/docs/government/org-admin/setup-wizard)**: finish setting up a new organization
* **[Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users)**: find users, change their role or seat tier, and check their usage
* **[Seats](/docs/government/org-admin/seats)**: see how many seats of each tier your organization has and how many are currently in use
* **[Tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers)**: review the Anthropic-managed seat tiers and create your own tiers with custom model access and spend limits
* **[Group mappings](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning)**: map directory groups to seat tiers and roles so that users added through your directory land in the right place automatically
* **[Analytics](/docs/government/org-admin/analytics)**: review requests, tokens, and top users over time across your organization
* **[Billing](/docs/government/org-admin/billing)**: see the billing account that funds your organization and any spend caps
* **[Readiness](/docs/government/org-admin/readiness)**: see what is blocking users from using Claude and where each item is resolved
* **[Config](/docs/government/org-admin/configuration)**: adjust product settings, such as which products members get, for everyone in your organization
* **[Compliance API](/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api)**: create and manage read-only API keys that stream your organization's audit events to a SIEM or log management system

The **Billing** and **Group mappings** tabs appear in the navigation only when they apply to your organization, and each of those pages says when.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Single sign-on and the SCIM provisioning connection are configured at the tenant level, so they are managed on the [tenant portal's Identity and access page](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access) rather than here. The routing rules that place people in your organization are managed there too, by tenant administrators.

## How changes take effect

Most changes you make in this portal take effect immediately. Changing a user's seat tier, updating a spend limit, or resetting a user's rate limits applies to their very next request. For when settings on the **Config** page reach your users' Claude applications, see [When changes take effect](/docs/government/config/overview#when-changes-take-effect).


# Group mappings
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning

Map directory groups to seat tiers and roles in your organization, and see how mappings are applied and what a deactivation in your directory does.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners who want directory groups to drive seat tiers and roles automatically.

Once a SCIM connection is in place, your directory groups appear here and you can map each one to a **seat tier** (a named level of access that determines which Claude models and usage limits a user gets) and a **role** (which controls whether a user can access this admin portal).

> [!NOTE]
>
> The **Group mappings** tab only appears in the navigation if automatic directory provisioning has been set up for your tenant. If you don't see the tab, your tenant administrator has not connected a directory. These cases are covered on other pages:
>
> * **SCIM connection**: the base URL and secret token are set up once for the whole tenant under [SCIM provisioning](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#scim-provisioning) on the tenant portal's Identity and access page
> * **Group to organization routing**: mapping directory groups to organizations is handled under [Provisioning rules](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#provisioning-rules-scim) on the same page

## Group to seat tier

To add a mapping, choose a group and a tier and click **Add**. Members of the group are moved to that tier, existing users included. To change a group's tier, click **Remove** on its mapping and add a new one. Each group can be mapped to at most one tier.

* **Someone who leaves a mapped group, or whose group's mapping is removed,** keeps the tier, with its models and spend limits, until another mapping or an owner moves them. On a tier with a seat limit, a [reconciliation](#how-mappings-are-applied) can move them too.
* **Mapping a group to a tier with a seat limit** can move other people off it. At a reconciliation, provisioned users on it who are in no mapped group can be moved to the tier in [step 3](/docs/government/org-admin/seats#how-seats-are-assigned-automatically) if it comes before theirs. On the tier marked **New members start here**, they stay.

If no groups have appeared at all, ask your tenant administrator to assign groups to the Claude for Government application in your identity provider and run a provisioning sync first.

## Group to role

Make your first role mapping a group that holds all your Owners, mapped to **Owner**. An Owner left out of it can lose access to this portal. You cannot map a group to Primary Owner; grant that role on the [Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users) page.

While this organization has no group-to-role mapping, members keep their roles unless a rule [moves them to another organization](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#when-rules-move-people). Once it has one, every member [linked to your directory](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#existing-accounts-when-you-connect-scim) except a Primary Owner gets their mapped role, or **User** if none of their groups is mapped. So you don't need to map any group to **User**.

## How mappings are applied

Each push from your identity provider is applied to your user list by a reconciliation pass.

* **After a mapping change.** Adding or removing a mapping starts a full reconciliation, so existing users are re-evaluated without waiting for your identity provider's next sync. In a very large directory, it can take hours.
* **Several mapped groups.** When a provisioned user belongs to several groups mapped to a seat tier, the one highest in your tenant's [group priority](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#directory-groups) decides. For roles, an order you can't see or change decides, and **User** can win over **Owner**. So don't map a group that includes your Owners, such as an all-staff group, to **User**.
* **No mapped group.** See [How seats are assigned automatically](/docs/government/org-admin/seats#how-seats-are-assigned-automatically).
* **No free seats.** If a new person's mapped or marked tier is full, provisioning doesn't add them yet. An existing member whose mapped tier is full keeps their current tier or stays **Unassigned**. They are tried again at each full reconciliation, which changing seat allocations or mappings starts, and when your directory updates their entry.

## What your directory controls

* Provisioning is the source of truth while it is connected. A seat tier (**Unassigned** included) or role you set manually on the [Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users) page can be overwritten on the next reconciliation. Make permanent changes in your directory or in your group mappings instead.
* Deactivating a user in your directory deactivates their linked account in Claude for Government and releases its seat, unless provisioning refuses the deactivation. Reactivating them in the directory reactivates them here if a seat is free for them. If they stay deactivated, free a seat for them, then deactivate and reactivate them in your directory.
* Provisioning will not deactivate or demote a Primary Owner, or deactivate your tenant's only active tenant administrator. To deactivate a Primary Owner, first change their role on the [Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users) page (if they are the only one, make someone else Primary Owner first), then have your directory send or resend the deactivation.
* Provisioning can also refuse to deactivate a user whose account is not yet linked to your directory: see [Existing accounts when you connect SCIM](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#existing-accounts-when-you-connect-scim).


# Readiness
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/readiness

Readiness checks for your organization: what the checks on credits, spend caps, seats, seat tiers, models, and products mean, and who can clear each one.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners who are setting up an organization for the first time, or who need to find out why their users are unable to use Claude.

The **Readiness** page shows what this organization still needs before its members can use Claude, and where each item is resolved. To open it, go to **Settings > Readiness** in the organization admin portal. You would normally work through it once when the organization is first set up and then return whenever the **Settings** menu shows a notification dot. The dot means a required step is unfinished.

The first unfinished required step explains why it is blocked, and either offers a button that takes you to the page where the fix is made or names who it is waiting on, such as **Waiting on Anthropic** or **Waiting on your tenant admin**. A step that isn't required doesn't raise the dot, but members can still be stuck until it is done.

Your tenant administrator can clear the steps that wait on them from the [tenant Readiness page](/docs/government/tenant-admin/readiness), which shows every organization's checklist in one place.

## What the checks mean

The table shows what a check means when it is unfinished, and who can clear it.

| Check | What it means | Who clears it |
| - | - | - |
| **Activate the organization** | This organization has been deactivated. While it is inactive its members cannot sign in and none of the other checks can be cleared. | Anthropic |
| **Assign a seat tier to the organization** | No seat tier is available to this organization. Until one is, no member can be given a seat. | You, or whoever the step names |
| **Add credits** | The billing account your organization draws from needs credits. Until it has them, every message from a user on a [self-managed tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#anthropic-managed-versus-self-managed-tiers) is refused. | Only Anthropic can add credits |
| **Raise the organization's spend cap** | A tenant administrator has set a spend cap on your organization that is too low to cover a request. Every request from a user on a self-managed tier is refused until the cap is raised or cleared. | Only a tenant administrator can change caps |
| **Assign a model to your seat tier** | No seat tier in this organization both allows a usable model and has usage limits high enough for one request, so nobody can send a message regardless of credits or seats. | You, on the [Seat tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) page, by adding a model or raising the tier's limits. Anthropic, for a tier you can't edit |
| **Allocate seats** | New members arrive without a seat and cannot send messages. | Your tenant administrator, or the organization that manages your billing account: see [Seats](/docs/government/org-admin/seats) |
| **Assign seat tiers to members** | An active member has no seat tier, and a member without one cannot use Claude. | You, on the [Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users) page, when a seat is free. A member without a seat shows **Unassigned** there. See also [How seats are assigned automatically](/docs/government/org-admin/seats#how-seats-are-assigned-automatically) |
| **Enable a product** | No Claude product, such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or Claude for Microsoft 365, is enabled for this organization. With nothing enabled, no client application can start. | You or your tenant administrator, on the [Config](/docs/government/org-admin/configuration) page |


# Seat tiers
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers

Seat tiers set which Claude models a user can access and how much they can spend. Organization owners create and manage their own seat tiers.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners who need to review the seat tiers available to their organization or define their own.

A **seat tier** bundles together which Claude models a user may access and how much they may spend in a given period. Every user sits on exactly one tier (or is unassigned), and the tier they hold controls their day-to-day limits. The **Tiers** page lists every tier available to your organization. To open it, go to **People > Tiers** in the [organization admin portal](/docs/government/org-admin/overview#who-can-access-it). Tenant administrators reach that portal through **Switch to org view** in the tenant view's footer.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These tasks are covered on other pages:
>
> * **Put a user on a tier**: see [Assigning a seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/users#assigning-a-seat-tier)
> * **Turn a Claude product on or off**: see [Product availability](/docs/government/config/settings#product-availability)

The tiers your organization creates are **self-managed tiers**. They draw from the credits in the [billing account](/docs/government/org-admin/billing) your organization spends from, so requests from people on them are refused while the account has no credits or your organization has reached a spend cap. They have no seat limit unless one is set.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Anthropic-managed tiers.** If your agency buys seats, Anthropic sets up your tiers, and you don't need to create any. You can't delete an Anthropic-managed tier or change what it allows, and its spend limits aren't shown. To start new members on one, go to **People > Tiers**, open the tier, select [**New members start here**](/docs/government/org-admin/seats#how-seats-are-assigned-automatically), and click **Save**. These tiers don't draw from credits, so people on them keep working while the account has none.

## Creating a self-managed tier

You can create, edit, and delete self-managed tiers only if your tenant has [allowed organizations to manage their own seat tiers](/docs/government/config/settings#let-organizations-manage-their-own-seat-tiers). Go to **People > Tiers**, click **New seat tier**, and fill in the form. If you don't see the button, a tenant administrator can turn on that setting. If it is already on, contact your Anthropic representative.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Make sure your [billing account](/docs/government/org-admin/billing) has credits before anyone is placed on the tier, or their requests are refused.

* **Five-hour spend limit** sets how much each user on this tier can spend in a 5-hour window, expressed in dollars. When a user reaches this amount, further requests are refused until the limit [resets](/docs/government/account/usage#reading-the-reset-times).
* **Seven-day spend limit** does the same for a 7-day window. Both limits apply at the same time, so whichever is reached first stops the user.
* **Allowed models** controls which [Claude models](/docs/government/desktop/models) users on this tier may use. If you leave it empty, users on the tier have no model access regardless of their spend limits.
* **Default model** sets the model that new chats, tasks, and Code sessions in Claude Desktop start on, chosen from the tier's allowed models. It applies to users who haven't picked a model or effort level in the model picker.
* Select **Always start with the default model** to start every new chat, task, and Code session on the default model. Requires a **Default model** and Claude Desktop 2.110.0 or later.
* **New members start here** makes this the tier that people start on when they join your organization, as described under [How seats are assigned automatically](/docs/government/org-admin/seats#how-seats-are-assigned-automatically). Turning it on here turns it off for any other tier. On a tier with a seat limit and a mapped group, turning it off can move provisioned users who are in no mapped group [to another tier](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#group-to-seat-tier).

## Viewing and editing a tier

Go to **People > Tiers**, open a self-managed tier, and use its **Edit** form.

* Changes to spend limits and allowed models take effect immediately for every user on the tier: if you lower the spend limit, a user who is already over the new limit will be blocked on their next request until the limit resets, and if you remove a model from **Allowed models** it becomes unavailable to every user on the tier straight away.
* Changes to **Default model** and **Always start with the default model** reach users when Claude Desktop next [refreshes its configuration](/docs/government/config/overview#when-changes-take-effect), and a new default appears the next time they start Claude Desktop. When you set or change a tier's **Default model**, Claude Desktop prompts users on that tier who have the app open [to restart](/docs/government/config/settings#restart-deadline-for-configuration-changes). To avoid the prompt, set a tier's **Default model** before its users first open Claude Desktop.

If a banner that begins **Anthropic has provided default seat tiers** appears in the organization admin portal, Anthropic has set up a self-managed seat tier for your organization to review. Click **Review seat tiers**, then adjust the tier in the **Edit** form and click **Save**, or click **Keep these values**.

## Deleting a tier

Go to **People > Tiers**, open a self-managed tier, and click **Delete** to remove it entirely. Deletion is permanent.

If any users are still assigned to it, or any group mapping on the [Group mappings](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning) page points at it, the delete is refused. Reassign or remove those references first, then delete the tier.


# Seats
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/seats

See how many seats of each tier your organization holds and how many are assigned, and how new and unassigned users get a seat tier.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners who need to see how many seats of each tier are available and how many are in use.

The **Seats** page shows how many seats your organization has for each [seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#the-tier-list) and how many of them are currently assigned to users. For each tier, **Assigned** is how many of your users are on that tier, and **Limit** is the number of seats your organization has been allocated. You cannot assign more users to a tier than its limit allows, and a self-managed tier [may have no limit](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#anthropic-managed-versus-self-managed-tiers). The **Assigned** count includes only [active users](/docs/government/org-admin/users#deactivated-users).

> [!NOTE]
>
> The **Seats** page is read-only. These tasks are covered on other pages:
>
> * **Move a user onto a different tier**: use the [Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users#assigning-a-seat-tier) page
> * **Create or edit self-managed tiers**: use the [Tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) page
> * **Change how many seats your organization holds**: ask a [tenant administrator](/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats#change-seat-allocations), unless your organization manages its own billing account. Then a [Primary Owner](/docs/government/org-admin/users#understanding-roles) uses [Seats](/docs/government/org-admin/billing#seats) on the Billing page.

## How seats are assigned automatically

Someone who joins your organization gets the first of these that applies:

1. The tier one of their directory groups is [mapped to](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#group-to-seat-tier).
2. The tier marked **New members start here** on the [Tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) page.
3. The tier with a **Limit**, a free seat, and the lowest **Sort order**.

If their mapped or marked tier is full, they get no seat, even if another tier has one free. If a full tier is the reason, someone new from your directory [isn't added yet](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#how-mappings-are-applied).

Anyone else with no seat is **Unassigned** and has no model access. Adding more seats later seats only those of them in a mapped group. For the rest, an owner can [choose a tier](/docs/government/org-admin/users#assigning-a-seat-tier), and so can a tenant administrator from your organization's admin view.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Tiers with a seat limit.** A self-managed tier has no **Limit** unless one is set for it. People who hold a seat stay put when a **Limit** or **Sort order** changes, though [mapping groups to tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#group-to-seat-tier) can move some.


# Setup wizard
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/setup-wizard

Setup wizard for a new organization: how to open it, and what the seat tiers, seats and credits, products, and finish steps cover.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners setting up a newly created organization, or returning to finish setup later.

When a tenant administrator creates your organization and names you as its primary owner, a few things still need to be in place before your team can use Claude. The setup wizard walks you through those items in order, shows you which ones are already done, and tells you when something is waiting on someone else.

Until setup is complete, a banner reading **A few steps remain before your team can use Claude** appears in the organization admin portal. Click **Resume setup** in that banner to open the wizard. The banner goes away once every required item is complete, and it reappears on its own if a required item later becomes incomplete, for example if a spend cap is set too low.

Use **Continue later** on any step to leave the wizard, and come back through the banner whenever you are ready. The wizard makes the same changes as the matching pages in the admin portal.

## Wizard steps

* **Welcome.** Single sign-on and provisioning are configured by your tenant administrator rather than here, so your members will appear in this organization once they sign in through the tenant's identity provider, if your tenant administrator's routing rules send them here.
* **Seat tiers.** This step lists every tier available to your organization. See [Seat tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#creating-a-self-managed-tier) for more on creating and editing tiers.
* **Seats & credits.** [Seats](/docs/government/org-admin/seats) are allocated outside the wizard, and Anthropic adds credits to the [billing account](/docs/government/org-admin/billing) your organization draws from, so this step is a status display rather than a form. Each line is a check from the [Readiness](/docs/government/org-admin/readiness#what-the-checks-mean) page and names who it is waiting on.
* **Products.** These are the Claude products your members sign in to, such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Claude for Microsoft 365. Turning a product on allows your members to sign in to that application, unless your tenant administrator has turned it off for the whole tenant. This step is marked **Optional** in the step list. A product that is not available appears with its switch disabled and a note to contact Anthropic. You can change these switches later from the [Config](/docs/government/org-admin/configuration) page.
* **Finish.** The final step shows the full readiness checklist for your organization. For what the checks mean, see [Readiness](/docs/government/org-admin/readiness#what-the-checks-mean).


# Users
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/org-admin/users

Find a user, change their role or seat tier, sign them out everywhere, check and reset their usage limits, and see what each organization role can do.

> **Who this is for:** Organization owners who need to manage individual users' roles, seat tiers, and usage limits.

The **Users** page lists everyone in your organization and lets you manage their access. Use **Filters** to narrow the list by role or seat tier, or to include deactivated accounts.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These cases are covered on other pages:
>
> * **Adding people to your organization**: see [How people get access](/docs/government/overview#how-people-get-access)
> * **Users your directory provisions**: provisioning can overwrite a role or seat tier you set here, **Unassigned** included, as described under [What your directory controls](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#what-your-directory-controls)

## Understanding roles

A **role** controls what a person can do in the admin portal. It has no effect on which Claude models they can use or how much they can use them; those are controlled by the [seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers).

* A **User** can use the Claude products but has no admin access.
* An **Owner** can access this organization admin portal and manage its users, seats, and settings.
* A **Primary Owner** can do everything an Owner can, and can grant or remove the Primary Owner role.

There are no additional roles such as Billing or Developer. Tenant administrator access is a separate tenant-level membership managed on the [Admins](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins) page, not an organization role.

An organization may have up to three active Primary Owners. If your organization no longer has a Primary Owner who can sign in, ask a tenant administrator to promote a replacement, unless your organization [manages its own billing account](/docs/government/org-admin/billing#seats). If it does, contact Anthropic instead to have a new Primary Owner appointed. Until then, your Owners and tenant administrators can keep managing users and settings.

## Change a role

Use the **Role** dropdown on a user's card to change their role. The change applies immediately, and a user who is promoted to Owner can open the admin portal as soon as they refresh.

The following safeguards apply and the dropdown will refuse the change if any of them would be violated.

* You cannot change your own role.
* An Owner can freely move people between User and Owner, but can't grant or remove the Primary Owner role. A Primary Owner can grant or remove it. A tenant administrator can too, unless your organization [manages its own billing account](/docs/government/org-admin/billing#seats).
* You cannot demote the organization's only active Primary Owner. Promote a second person to Primary Owner first, then demote the original.
* You cannot promote a deactivated user to Primary Owner. Reactivate them first.

## Assigning a seat tier

Use the **Seat tier** dropdown to move a user onto a different tier or back to **Unassigned**. An unassigned user has no model access at all, but keeps their account and any admin access. If a tier has no seats remaining it appears marked **(at capacity)** and cannot be selected, unless the user is already on it. Only a Primary Owner can change a Primary Owner's seat tier here. If one of the user's directory groups is mapped to another seat tier, the mapping puts them back on it, so first change the [mapping](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#group-to-seat-tier) or the user's groups.

Changing a user's tier takes effect on their very next request. If you move someone to a tier with a different set of allowed models, any model that is not among their new tier's allowed models becomes unavailable to them immediately. Moving a user between tiers does not reset their usage counters, which are measured against the new tier's limit on their next request.

## Reset usage limits

Every [seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) sets a **5-hour** and a **7-day** spend limit for each user. When a user reaches either limit, further requests are refused until that limit resets. The **Usage** bars on a user's card show how much of the user's 5-hour and 7-day spend limits are currently used. Hover over the bars to see when each limit resets.

If a user on a self-managed tier has hit a limit and you want them to continue working immediately, use **Reset usage limits** in the **…** menu on their card. This clears both of their current windows so their next request is admitted. Their usage still shows on the [Analytics](/docs/government/org-admin/analytics) page.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You cannot reset limits for users on [Anthropic-managed tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#anthropic-managed-versus-self-managed-tiers).

## Sign out everywhere

The **…** menu on each card has **Sign out everywhere**, which ends every session the user has open, in the browser and in Claude apps on all their devices. They can sign in again unless their account is deactivated.

## Deactivated users

Accounts are deactivated through your directory's SCIM provisioning rather than from this page. A deactivated user cannot sign in. Deactivating a user releases their [seat](/docs/government/org-admin/seats). Reactivating them brings the account back if a seat is free for them, as described under [What your directory controls](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#what-your-directory-controls).

Deactivated users keep their role. Deactivating a user leaves their Claude Desktop conversations and projects on the devices they used. To remove them, see [Removing data](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage#removing-data) in the Claude Desktop documentation.

## Copy user email addresses

To email everyone in your organization, select the **Copy user email addresses** button at the top of the **Users** page. The page that opens lists every user's email address except deactivated users.


# Claude for Government administrator guide
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/overview

Set up and manage Claude for Government for your agency: how tenants, organizations, users, seats, and credits fit together.

> **Who this guide is for:** Administrators who set up and manage Claude for Government for their agency.

This guide covers the portals used to manage Claude for Government: how access, seats, and usage are organized, and who is responsible for each part. Members use Claude in the Claude apps, such as Claude Desktop, that your agency [makes available](/docs/government/config/settings#product-availability). Claude for Government isn't available in the Claude mobile apps.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These cases are covered on other pages:
>
> * **Managing your whole tenant**: see [Tenant administration](/docs/government/tenant-admin/overview)
> * **Managing one organization**: see [Organization administration](/docs/government/org-admin/overview)
> * **Setting up a new tenant**: see [Tenant setup wizard](/docs/government/tenant-admin/setup-wizard)
> * **Checking your own profile, usage, or sessions**: see [Your account](/docs/government/account/overview)
> * **Using Claude Desktop**: see [Video walkthroughs for Claude Desktop](/docs/government/desktop/video-walkthroughs)
> * **Installing Claude Desktop on agency devices**: see [Connect Claude Desktop to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure)
> * **Reviewing security and data handling**: see [Security and data handling](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling)

## How your deployment is organized

Claude for Government is organized as a three-level hierarchy:

* **Tenant**: The tenant is the top level, and it represents your agency's overall deployment. The tenant is managed by a short list of [tenant administrators](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins).
* **Organizations**: An organization is a group of users who share a pool of seats and a set of policies, with its own spend caps. Each organization has its own owners, its own members, its own seat assignments, and its own configuration. The organizations all share the tenant's single sign-on connection, so you configure identity once and every organization uses it.
* **Users**: A user never belongs to more than one organization at a time. Each user has a [role](/docs/government/org-admin/users#understanding-roles), which decides what they can manage, and a [seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers), which decides which models they can use and how much. A user with no seat tier can sign in and see their account, but they can't send messages to Claude.

You might create one organization for each bureau, office, or program, or you might run the whole agency as a single organization. You would create more when you need any of the following:

* Separate billing accounts so one group's usage never draws down another group's balance
* Separate usage reporting for each bureau or program
* Different product settings, seat tiers, or access rules for different parts of your agency

A **billing account** is where your agency's credits and seats live. Anthropic sets up one or more billing accounts with your agency. Every organization is linked to exactly one billing account. Several organizations can share the same billing account, or each organization can have its own. Tenant administrators divide each billing account's [seat pool](/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats#how-seats-are-organized) among the organizations it funds, and can set per-organization [spend caps](/docs/government/tenant-admin/credits) to control how much any one organization draws from a shared balance.

## The three views

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Finding your way around" />

Video: Finding your way around (2 min 24 s). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

[Transcript](/docs/government/video-walkthroughs#finding-your-way-around)

Open the portal in a browser at your agency's Claude for Government address followed by `/gateway`. Which views you can reach depends on your role, and you switch between them using the link in the page footer.

* [**Tenant**](/docs/government/tenant-admin/overview): tenant administrators
* [**Organization admin**](/docs/government/org-admin/overview): organization owners and tenant administrators
* [**Account**](/docs/government/account/overview): everyone

Organization owners land on the organization admin view, and members with no administrative role land on their account view. Tenant administrators reach the tenant view from the **Switch to tenant view** link in the organization admin view's footer.

Being a [tenant administrator](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins#how-tenant-admin-access-works) is separate from the role you hold inside an organization.

## How people get access

A tenant administrator connects your agency's [single sign-on](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#single-sign-on) and, optionally, [directory provisioning (SCIM)](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#scim-provisioning) on the [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access) page. [Routing rules](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#routing-rules) then decide which organization each person joins. A new person who does not match any rule cannot sign in until a rule is added that covers them. A rule change can also move people who already have an account, as described in [When rules move people](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#when-rules-move-people).


# Security and data handling
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling

Review how Claude for Government handles data: sandbox isolation, network traffic, approvals, connector credentials, telemetry, web search, and local storage.

> **Who this is for:** Security, compliance, and IT reviewers who are assessing Claude for Government for their agency, and administrators who need to explain the product's runtime behavior.

The answers on this page address the security and data-handling questions that come up most often during agency security review, for the [Claude Desktop application](#claude-desktop) and for the standalone [Claude Code command-line tool](#claude-code-command-line-tool), each in its own section. For assurance materials such as the security architecture overview, SOC 2 Type 2 report, and penetration testing summary, request access through the [Anthropic Trust Center](https://trust.anthropic.com).

> [!NOTE]
>
> These cases are covered on other pages:
>
> * **What each setting does**: see [Available settings](/docs/government/config/settings)
> * **Installing the app and managing it on devices**: see [Connect Claude Desktop to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure)

## Claude Desktop

The sections below cover the Claude Desktop application, which offers three ways to work with Claude: **Chat** for simple conversations, **Cowork** for longer tasks with a local workspace folder, and **Code** for software development. With the [**Standard** home](/docs/government/config/settings#claude-desktop-home), a message sent from the home screen [starts a Cowork session](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/unified-claude#what-users-see-with-unified-claude) on a device that can run Cowork.

### Sandbox and isolation

In Cowork, and for the file-analysis steps in Chat, the Claude Desktop application runs shell commands and model-written code inside a dedicated local virtual machine. In Claude for Government, this sandbox is always the execution path for the code and shell commands that Claude runs in Chat and Cowork. The agent loop, built-in file tools, web fetch, and the connector client run in the Claude Desktop application on the user's device. Code sessions run on the workstation itself rather than in the virtual machine, as described under [Code in Claude Desktop](#code-in-claude-desktop). For the detailed threat model and isolation design, request the security architecture overview through the [Anthropic Trust Center](https://trust.anthropic.com).

Shell commands that Claude runs in the sandbox work on the folders the user has attached, a scratch area, and read-only reference material (such as skill and plugin directories). Shell commands cannot work on the rest of the user's files.

* **Attached folders.** When a user attaches a local folder to a Cowork session, the entire folder is made available to that session's sandbox as a filesystem mount, so changes Claude makes are written directly to the folder on disk. For mapped drives, see [Network drives on Windows](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/local-access#network-drives-on-windows).
* **Attached files.** Files the user attaches individually to a conversation are copied or hard-linked into a per-conversation uploads directory and mounted read-only; where the filesystem hard-links, edits to the original file while the conversation is open can be visible to it.
* **Folder restrictions.** Administrators can restrict which local folders users may attach with **Allowed workspace folders** on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#allowed-workspace-folders) page. The desktop client then refuses folders outside that list in the workspace picker, in requests Claude makes during a session, and in Claude's file tools. In Cowork, Claude's file tools may read and write in the listed folders. See [Desktop and filesystem access](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/local-access) for how folder scoping is enforced.
* **File analysis in Chat.** Some attachment types, such as Excel and PowerPoint, need a conversion step that runs inside the sandbox. See [**Advanced file analysis in Chat**](/docs/government/config/settings#advanced-file-analysis-in-chat). You do not need to make Cowork available to get this capability. See [Chat in Claude Desktop](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/chat#advanced-file-analysis) for how Chat handles file attachments.

### Code in Claude Desktop

Code sessions use Claude Code built into the desktop application and run on the user's workstation itself, not in the virtual machine. The shell commands Claude runs during a Code session execute on the workstation's own operating system under the user's own account.

On macOS and Linux, those shell commands run inside an operating-system-level sandbox that the application builds from your organization's **Allowed network hosts** and **Allowed workspace folders** settings on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#allowed-network-hosts) page. The sandbox is in place whenever either setting restricts access, which the default configuration does. Inside the sandbox, a command can create or change files in the session's folder, the other folders **Allowed workspace folders** permits, and temporary locations. Unless [**Block reads outside workspace folders**](/docs/government/config/settings#block-reads-outside-workspace-folders) (Claude Desktop 1.46388.1 or later) is on, it can read any file on the device that the user's account can open. By default it runs without asking the user first. A user can [exempt specific commands from this sandbox](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#run-commands-outside-the-sandbox-with-excludedcommands) in a Claude Code settings file, and an exempted command runs outside the sandbox under the [permission mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) the user selects for the session. In their own Claude Code settings, a user can also [widen which files sandboxed commands can read or change](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#configure-sandboxing). The sandbox limits Claude, not a user who chooses to loosen it.

* **Windows.** On Windows, there is no operating-system-level sandbox for Code sessions. Shell commands run directly on the device under the [permission mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) the user selects for the session and under your agency's own endpoint and network controls. The **Allowed network hosts** and **Allowed workspace folders** settings do not confine what those commands can reach, read, or change.
* **Linux.** On Linux, the sandbox requires the `bubblewrap` and `socat` packages, so install both on each workstation as described under [Set up Linux and WSL2](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#set-up-linux-and-wsl2) in the Claude Code documentation. If either package is missing or the sandbox cannot start, shell commands can run outside it, as they do on Windows.
* **Container workspaces.** In container-based Linux environments, such as cloud development workspaces, the sandbox can fail to start, and shell commands in Code sessions can then fail with a `bwrap` error. To run Code sessions there, set **Shell command sandbox** to **Off** under **Advanced settings** in the **Claude Code** section of the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#shell-command-sandbox) page, at the level that applies to the members who work in those environments, such as a [directory group](/docs/government/config/overview#group-specific-settings). **Off** applies to those members on every device they use, not only in the container workspaces. It reaches their Code sessions where your organization's [Claude Code settings](/docs/government/config/settings#claude-code) do. Shell commands in those Code sessions then run without the sandbox, under the permission mode the user selects for the session, as they do on Windows, and the **Allowed network hosts** and **Allowed workspace folders** settings no longer confine what those commands can reach or change. **Off** also turns the sandbox off in those members' sessions in the Claude Code command-line tool.
* **The terminal.** Claude's terminal tools type commands into the Code tab's terminal, which is the user's own shell (PowerShell on Windows). The app asks the user to approve each of those commands by default, and they run as the user, outside any sandbox. On macOS and Linux, Claude Desktop 4.23118.0 or later offers these tools in local sessions only where neither **Allowed network hosts** nor **Allowed workspace folders** restricts access. Administrators can turn these terminal tools off with the **Terminal panel tools** card on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#terminal-panel-tools) page. The [**Blocked shell commands**](/docs/government/config/settings#blocked-shell-commands) list does not block commands Claude types into the terminal, but the **Require approval for each command** sub-setting on the **Shell commands** card applies to them in every permission mode.
* **Folders and approval.** On every operating system, the application starts a Code session only in a folder that **Allowed workspace folders** permits when that setting is configured, and Claude's file reading and editing tools then work only inside the permitted folders. Administrators can also require a prompt before Claude uses its shell tool, with the [**Require approval for each command**](/docs/government/config/settings#require-approval-for-each-command) sub-setting on the **Shell commands** card.
* **Remote and WSL sessions.** Code sessions in Claude for Government run on the local workstation by default. SSH remote sessions are off unless your agency allows specific hosts in Claude Code's managed settings on the device; see [Interaction with Claude Code managed settings on the device](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/ssh-remote-sessions#interaction-with-claude-code-managed-settings-on-the-device). On Windows devices set up through device management, Code sessions inside a Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) distribution are [off by default](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#disablewslsessions).
* **Local sockets.** A command that talks to a local agent through a socket, such as git signing a commit with a key held in an SSH agent or a hardware-backed key manager, cannot reach that agent from inside the sandbox. On macOS, a user who needs such a command to work can list the agent's socket path under `sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets` in their Claude Code settings file, which keeps the command inside the sandbox. Every sandboxed command in that user's Code sessions can then ask the agent to sign or authenticate. A sandboxed command can change files that git runs during a commit, such as hook scripts kept in the working tree, and a `git commit` exempted with `sandbox.excludedCommands` runs that code outside the sandbox. See [Sandbox settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-settings) in the Claude Code documentation.

See [how your configuration reaches Code sessions](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/code).

If your agency also deploys Claude Code's own managed settings to the same devices:

* **Where your organization's [Claude Code settings](/docs/government/config/settings#claude-code) reach Code sessions**: Claude Code uses them instead of the Claude Code policy in those managed settings, such as hooks and permission rules, apart from the [keys Claude Code reads from every admin source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-read-from-every-admin-source). The restrictions Claude Desktop [applies as managed policy](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/code#applied-as-managed-policy) also apply, except where your organization's settings override them.
* **Where they don't**: whether the restrictions Claude Desktop [applies as managed policy](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/code#applied-as-managed-policy), the sandbox included, still apply beside those managed settings depends on their `parentSettingsBehavior`. [Interaction with Claude Code's own managed settings](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/code#interaction-with-claude-code%E2%80%99s-own-managed-settings) explains each value.

### Network egress, required domains, and proxies

You manage the egress allowlist with the **Allowed network hosts** setting on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#allowed-network-hosts) page.

For configuration and model inference, the application reaches the Claude for Government service hostname provided to your agency during onboarding. Sign-in happens in the user's default browser, which must reach that same hostname, the Claude for Government sign-in service (a separate host that your Anthropic representative provides), and your agency's identity provider. See the network prerequisites in [Connect Claude Desktop to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#network-access). Claude for Government does not publish IP addresses for its service and sign-in hosts. The [IP addresses](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/ip-addresses) page in the Claude API documentation covers the Claude API, not the Claude for Government hosts. Anthropic-bound telemetry endpoints are not contacted in Claude for Government. The app also reaches the hosts listed under Non-essential services in [Required egress paths](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/telemetry#required-egress-paths). If traffic is blocked, the app will run without icons, previews, and widgets.

* **Does Claude for Government depend on claude.ai or anthropic.com?** Sign-in, configuration, and model inference do not: none of the hosts they use are under either domain. Blocking `*.claude.ai` and `*.anthropic.com` leaves sign-in and inference working. Blocking `*.claude.ai` also blocks `downloads.claude.ai`, which prevents Chat conversations, Cowork tasks, and Code sessions from starting on devices installed with the standard installer unless the app has already downloaded the components they need from that host. App updates often change one or both of those components, and the sandbox virtual machine that runs shell commands in Cowork and Advanced file analysis in Chat then cannot start until the app has downloaded the new versions from that host. Devices installed with the offline installer variant, which includes those components, are not affected. On Claude Desktop versions earlier than 1.37937.0, [web fetch in Code sessions](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/web-tools#web-fetch) first sends the page's hostname to `api.anthropic.com` and fails where that host is blocked. Automatic application updates use hosts under these domains, so an agency that blocks these domains distributes updates itself, as described under [Automatic updates](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#automatic-updates). The hosts are listed under Auto-updates in [Required egress paths](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/telemetry#required-egress-paths). See [**Block automatic updates**](/docs/government/config/settings#block-automatic-updates) and [**Restart deadline for updates**](/docs/government/config/settings#restart-deadline-for-updates). A personal Claude account cannot sign in to Claude for Government, and a Claude for Government account cannot sign in to `claude.ai`, so there is no shared sign-in surface to restrict.
* **Egress allowlist.** The allowlist governs outbound network access from the shell commands and package installs of Cowork sessions, which run in the sandbox virtual machine, from the sandboxed shell commands of Code sessions on macOS and Linux (see [Code in Claude Desktop](#code-in-claude-desktop)), and from the host-side web fetch tool in Chat and Cowork.
