It does not govern web search (which routes through the Claude for Government service) or connector traffic (covered under [Connectors](#connectors) below). When the list is empty or unset, package installs and page fetches from those tools fail. On Claude Desktop versions earlier than 2.37337.0, those tools can still reach the Claude for Government service address and, if you have set a **Telemetry endpoint** on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#telemetry-endpoint) page, that collector's host. The list accepts exact hostnames, wildcard patterns such as `*.example.com`, or `*` to allow all outbound traffic. See [Web search and web fetch](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/web-tools) for the full allowlist semantics.
* **Proxies.** The desktop application [follows the operating system's proxy settings](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/network-proxy), including PAC URLs. Where no proxy settings reach the Cowork sandbox, as on Linux, its commands connect directly. See [Network proxy](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/network-proxy#traffic-that-bypasses-the-app-proxy) for the traffic that bypasses the proxy. TLS inspection at your proxy should work; validate this in your environment before rollout. Web search requests pass through your proxy to the Claude for Government service, and the service's onward call to the search provider originates from inside the FedRAMP High boundary.

### Approvals and Auto mode

By default, Claude for Government prompts the user for connector actions, for each web search, and, in Cowork, when Claude asks to add another folder to the session. In Chat and Cowork, Claude's file tools do not write outside the attached folders, the session's working folder, [memory](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage#memory), and the folders listed in [**Allowed workspace folders**](/docs/government/config/settings#allowed-workspace-folders). In Chat and Cowork, shell commands run without a prompt because they run inside the sandbox virtual machine. Web page fetches run without a prompt in both Chat and Cowork and are checked against the [egress allowlist](#network-egress-required-domains-and-proxies).

For most tools, users who see an approval prompt can choose **Always allow**, which suppresses that prompt for them going forward. Turning on the **Require approval for each search**, **Require approval for each fetch**, or **Require approval for each command** sub-setting on the **Web search**, **Web fetch**, or **Shell commands** card stops **Always allow** from suppressing that tool's prompts. In Chat on Claude Desktop versions earlier than 2.110.0, every shell command prompts regardless.

By default, members cannot switch to [Auto mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes), which Cowork shows as **Automatically approve**. When an administrator sets the **Auto mode** setting to **Allowed** on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#auto-mode) page, Claude Desktop offers it in Cowork and in Code sessions, and members can switch the Claude Code command-line tool to it. New Code sessions in Claude Desktop 2.9939.2 or later and new interactive sessions in the Claude Code command-line tool 2.1.283 or later then start in it on models that support Auto mode, unless another mode is chosen. Cowork does not offer a bypass-permissions mode. For Code sessions and the command-line tool, see [**Bypass-permissions mode**](/docs/government/config/settings#bypass-permissions-mode).

* **Connectors an administrator adds.** For each connector an administrator adds, the administrator can switch individual tools on or off under **Tool policy**. A tool that is on stays available and each user approves every use. A tool that is off is blocked. Users cannot loosen these settings. Tools that are not listed in a connector's **Tool policy**, including tools the server adds later, stay under each user's control.
* **[Microsoft 365 connector](/docs/government/connectors/microsoft-365).** The Microsoft 365 connector always asks for approval before write actions such as sending mail, changing calendar events, or posting Teams messages, and no Claude for Government setting removes that prompt. The **Microsoft 365** card has no per-tool setting, and the connector's read tools follow each user's own approval choices.
* **Can individual shell commands be allowlisted enterprise-wide?** Not in Chat or Cowork. Administrators can turn the built-in **Web search**, **Web fetch**, and **Shell commands** tools on or off, or require approval for them, but cannot allowlist individual commands within those tools. In Code sessions, the [Claude Code](/docs/government/config/settings#claude-code) section has no list of allowed commands. Permission rules in a Claude Code managed-settings file on the device can allow individual commands, but they apply in Code sessions only where your organization's Claude Code settings don't reach them, as [Code in Claude Desktop](#code-in-claude-desktop) describes.
* **Can Auto mode be disabled when a sensitive connector is attached?** Not for one connector alone. To limit a sensitive connector while Auto mode is allowed, switch the connector's tools off under **Tool policy** on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#tool-and-connector-cards) page.

See [Connector tool policies for members](/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors#connector-tool-policies-for-members), [Tool and connector cards](/docs/government/config/settings#tool-and-connector-cards), and [Connectors](/docs/government/connectors/overview) for the available settings.

### Connectors

Connectors are called from the desktop application, outside the sandbox. The [built-in Microsoft 365 connector](/docs/government/connectors/microsoft-365#allow-outbound-network-access) and [administrator-added connectors](/docs/government/connectors/overview) call their endpoints directly from the user's device, through the system proxy where one is configured. OAuth tokens for both are stored encrypted on each user's device using operating system encryption (macOS Keychain on Mac, DPAPI on Windows). A user's sign-in to a server that a plugin declares is stored differently, and on Windows and Linux it is not encrypted: see [Credentials](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage#credentials). For administrator-added connectors, the bearer header entered on the Config page is delivered to each user's desktop.

The **Let members add their own connectors** switch on the Config page controls whether end users can add local MCP servers of their own in Claude Desktop, under **Settings**, then **Developer**. It is off by default, as described under [Let members add their own connectors](/docs/government/config/settings#let-members-add-their-own-connectors). The [**Let members add plugin marketplaces**](/docs/government/config/settings#let-members-add-plugin-marketplaces) and [**Let members add their own plugins**](/docs/government/config/settings#let-members-add-their-own-plugins) switches on the Config page are off by default. Both need Claude Desktop 1.37937.0 or later; on earlier versions members can add marketplaces and plugins. Hook commands and local MCP servers run as programs under the user's own account, outside both the [sandbox virtual machine](#sandbox-and-isolation) and the [Code session sandbox](#code-in-claude-desktop). For the plugins an administrator adds, see [Plugins that run code](/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors#plugins-that-run-code).

Artifacts follow the same tool settings as Claude's direct connector calls: a connector tool that an administrator has switched off is refused, and a tool that requires approval on every use never runs from an artifact without the user's approval of that call.

### Telemetry and logging

In Claude for Government, Anthropic-bound error and usage telemetry is always disabled. The OpenTelemetry export to your own collector is a separate setting and sends data only to the endpoint you configure. You set the OpenTelemetry endpoint with **Telemetry endpoint** on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#telemetry-endpoint) page. The **Telemetry content capture** setting on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#telemetry-content-capture) page adds prompt, response, and tool content to the export for the categories you select, and nothing is selected by default.

**Is there an inline DLP or inspection point?** No. Claude for Government does not include an inline content-inspection or DLP gate. Claude for Government doesn't support routing Claude Desktop through an LLM gateway that your agency runs, and it doesn't issue API keys for model requests. The available inspection points are your own network proxy, which sees the traffic routed through it, and the desktop's OpenTelemetry export, which sends tool-call metadata (tool name, connector, outcome, duration, and approval status) to your collector for after-the-fact review. See [Telemetry and egress](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/telemetry) for what the export can include.

Chat and Cowork sessions write a [local audit log](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage#session-audit-log) to the user's disk recording prompt text, Claude's responses, tool inputs and results, and permission decisions. The app doesn't send that log off the device. Server-side, the [Compliance API](/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api) records identity and configuration events but never tool calls or conversation content.

### Data storage and retention

In Claude for Government, conversation content stays on the user's device. If you select content categories in the **Telemetry content capture** setting on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#telemetry-content-capture) page, Claude Desktop also sends the selected prompt, response, and tool content to your own OpenTelemetry collector, and never to Anthropic. Model requests are proxied through the Claude for Government service to the model endpoint inside the FedRAMP High boundary, and the service records only per-request metadata, not content.

* **Can Anthropic view conversations?** No. Chat transcripts are stored on the user's workstation, and the Claude for Government service does not log request or response bodies. Inference requests pass through the service to the model endpoint but are not retained.
* **Where on the device is conversation content stored?** Conversation content lives under the [application data directory](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage#where-data-lives) (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Claude-3p` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support/Claude-3p` on macOS, `~/.config/Claude-3p` on Linux). Code session transcripts live in Claude Code's own folder in the user's home directory (`~/.claude/projects`). The application does not encrypt these files itself, so encryption at rest depends on the workstation's full-disk encryption, such as BitLocker, FileVault, or LUKS. The operating system encryption that protects connector credentials, described under [Connectors](#connectors), does not apply to conversation content.
* **Is local history kept separate for each organization?** No. Claude Desktop keeps conversation history in the application data directory of the operating system account in use on the device, and it does not divide that history by the Claude for Government organization or tenant the user signs in to. A user who is moved to another organization, or who signs in to a second tenant from the same operating system account, sees the same conversations and projects as before. The Claude Desktop [configuration reference](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration#deploymentorganizationuuid) lists a `deploymentOrganizationUuid` key that separates local data by organization in other deployments. That key does not apply to Claude for Government, so leave it out of your [configuration profile](/docs/government/deploy-desktop/configure#deploy-to-your-fleet).
* **Projects.** A project in Claude for Government is stored in the application data directory on the user's own device, together with any instructions, links, and folder references the user adds to it. Files added to a project stay on the user's local disk; there is no service-side project store, and files are not vectorized or indexed. Claude reads them directly from disk on demand with its file tools. A new Cowork session in the project does not reuse what an earlier session read, so Claude reads the files it needs again. The project's [memory](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage#memory) carries short notes between sessions, such as preferences and decisions. Content Claude reads from those files is handled like the rest of the conversation: inference requests pass through the Claude for Government service to the model endpoint but are not retained.
* **Can the local data location be changed for backup or sync?** No. The location is fixed to the per-user application data directory, and the application avoids the roaming profile because the sandbox image cache can be large. Chat history exists only on the device that created it, so back up the application data directory through your endpoint management tools if you need to preserve it. [Removing data](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage#removing-data) describes how to clear it.

### Web search and web fetch

Web search is operated by Anthropic inside the Claude for Government FedRAMP High boundary, and the search provider's API is the one case where traffic egresses that boundary. Web search is built in and does not require obtaining a separate connector. Before search is enabled, an administrator must acknowledge a disclosure covering this data flow when enabling the **Web search** card on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#web-search) page. By default, users approve each query before it is sent, and Claude transforms it into a generic, de-identified search request and shows the user the exact text. The **Require approval for each search** setting is on by default. Anthropic has a zero-data-retention agreement with the search provider. The [Web search and web fetch](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/web-tools) page covers how web search is configured in other Claude Desktop deployments; the Claude for Government search path described here is specific to this deployment.

In Chat and Cowork, every web page fetch is checked against your egress allowlist before the request is made, and redirects are re-checked against the allowlist on each hop. See [Web search and web fetch](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/web-tools). Allowlist entries match by name, not by the address a name resolves to; see **Allowed network hosts** on the [Config](/docs/government/config/settings#allowed-network-hosts) page.

### Chat and Cowork differences

Chat and Cowork share one list of projects. Projects are not shared between users. Chat conversations in a project can read the project's [memory](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage#memory). See [Data storage and retention](#data-storage-and-retention) for where project contents are stored.

Artifacts are available in both Chat and Cowork. An artifact is an interactive page that Claude writes and the Claude Desktop application displays on the user's device, outside the sandbox, so artifacts remain available even when **Advanced file analysis in Chat** is off.

In Chat and Cowork, Claude creates files on the user's device in places such as these:

* A folder the user attached to a Cowork task.
* The working folder that each task or conversation has inside the [application data directory](#data-storage-and-retention).
* For artifacts, the user files directory (default `~/Claude`).

A user who wants results in a particular folder attaches that folder to the task and asks Claude to save the files there. Shell commands run inside the sandbox virtual machine, and on the device they can write only to the attached folders and the task's working folder. A file that a command writes anywhere else in the virtual machine, for example under `/tmp`, does not appear in any folder on the device. See [Chat in Claude Desktop](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/chat#what-a-chat-conversation-can-reach) for what a Chat conversation can reach, and [User identity and local data](/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/data-storage) for the folder layout.

## Claude Code command-line tool

The answers below cover the standalone Claude Code command-line tool when it signs in through Claude for Government, as [Connect Claude Code to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-claude-code/configure) describes. For Code sessions inside Claude Desktop, see [Code in Claude Desktop](#code-in-claude-desktop). For settings that govern the tool, such as [**Shell command sandbox**](/docs/government/config/settings#shell-command-sandbox), see [Claude Code](/docs/government/config/settings#claude-code) on the Available settings page.

* **Which domains does Claude Code need to reach?** The Claude for Government gateway address in the managed settings from [Connect Claude Code to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-claude-code/configure#the-managed-settings), over HTTPS on port 443, for sign-in, organization settings, and model inference. Sign-in finishes in the user's browser, which needs the Claude for Government host, its sign-in service, and your agency's identity provider, as for Claude Desktop. Claude Code also reaches, from the user's device, the address of each connector an administrator applies to **Claude Code** on the **Connectors** card, and that connector's sign-in service when it uses OAuth. The managed settings from [Connect Claude Code to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-claude-code/configure#before-sign-in) turn off Claude Code's background connections before sign-in (release notes, update checks, and the official plugin marketplace).
* **Does Claude Code send telemetry to Anthropic?** No. The managed settings in [Connect Claude Code to Claude for Government](/docs/government/deploy-claude-code/configure#the-managed-settings) turn off Claude Code's usage telemetry and error reporting to Anthropic from the first launch, and the organization's settings keep them off after sign-in.


# Admins
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins

Tenant administrator access: what it grants, who can be added, how to add or remove an administrator, and the safeguards on the list.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators who manage who else has tenant-level administrative access.

## How tenant admin access works

**Tenant administrator** is a specific membership list, separate from any role someone holds inside an organization. Being on this list grants access to every page in the tenant admin portal: creating organizations, configuring sign-in and provisioning, writing routing rules, distributing seats, setting spend caps, and setting tenant-wide configuration. It also lets the person open any organization's admin view and act on that organization's behalf.

Adding someone here doesn't make them an owner of any organization, and making someone an organization owner doesn't put them on this list. A tenant administrator doesn't have to belong to any organization or hold a seat. An administrator in no organization shows as **No organization** here and can't use Claude until they [join one](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#accounts-in-no-organization).

## Adding a tenant administrator

In the **Add admin** section, start typing a name or email address and select the person from the results, then click **Grant admin**. The change takes effect immediately; the next time that person loads the portal, the tenant admin view is available to them. Adding tenant administrators is self-service and does not require any action from Anthropic.

The search covers organization owners across every organization in your tenant, plus people in your tenant who don't belong to an organization. To add someone with the User role, make them an [Owner](/docs/government/org-admin/users#change-a-role) first. If their organization [maps directory groups to roles](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#group-to-role), add them to the group mapped to Owner in your directory instead.

## Removing a tenant administrator

Click **Remove** next to a name to revoke their tenant admin access. The change takes effect immediately. The person keeps their account and whatever organization role they have, but loses access to this portal. Unless they are an organization's [Primary Owner](/docs/government/org-admin/users#understanding-roles), they can also no longer use an [emailed sign-in link](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#emailed-sign-in-link).

* You can't remove the last remaining tenant administrator. This protects your tenant from losing all administrative access.
* You cannot remove yourself from the list. If your own access needs to be removed, ask another tenant administrator to do it.
* If the only person on this list leaves your agency or loses account access, contact Anthropic to have a new tenant administrator appointed.


# Config at the tenant level
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/configuration

Set tenant-wide defaults for product behavior, lock settings so organizations can't change them, and preview how a change affects each organization.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators who set and enforce product settings across every organization in their tenant.

In the tenant view of the admin portal, go to **Settings > Config** to set tenant-wide defaults for product behavior, [lock](/docs/government/config/overview#locks) settings so organizations can't change them, and [preview](/docs/government/config/overview#previewing-impact) how a change would affect each organization.

The Config page works the same way at the tenant and organization levels, with the same list of settings. See [How Config works](/docs/government/config/overview) for how levels, locks, and groups combine, and [Available settings](/docs/government/config/settings) for what each setting does.

To open an organization's Config page and act on that organization's behalf, select **Switch to org view**, choose the organization, and go to **Settings > Config**.


# Billing
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/credits

See each billing account's credit balance and set per-organization spend caps, with what a cap counts, what it stops, and when a change takes effect.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators who monitor billing-account balances and set spend caps on organizations.

The **Billing** page shows each billing account's **available balance**. This is also where you set per-organization spend caps, which limit how much any one organization can draw from its account.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The **Billing** tab appears in the navigation only when credits apply to your tenant.

## How billing works

A **billing account** is a funding pool that Anthropic sets up for your tenant. It holds a dollar balance of credit, and Anthropic adds credit to the account as part of your agency's procurement. Each organization is linked to exactly one billing account, and several organizations may share the same one. Usage on [self-managed seat tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#anthropic-managed-versus-self-managed-tiers) draws directly from the billing account's balance.

A spend cap limits how much one organization can spend from its billing account in a 5-hour or 7-day window.

* **What a cap counts.** Spend caps apply to usage on self-managed seat tiers. Usage on Anthropic-managed seat tiers is covered by the seat price rather than drawn from the account balance, so it is not counted against a cap.
* **Who is affected.** An organization that hits a spend cap does not affect other organizations on the same account. An account running out of balance stops usage on self-managed tiers in every organization on it. Low-balance alerts go to organization Owners and Primary Owners, as described under [Billing account](/docs/government/org-admin/billing#billing-account).
* **Who sets caps.** Spend caps are set by tenant administrators. Organization owners can see their own caps on their organization's [Billing](/docs/government/org-admin/billing) page, but cannot change them.

## Setting a spend cap

In a billing account's **Spend caps** section, click an organization's row to expand the editor, enter a dollar amount for the **5-hour cap**, the **7-day cap**, or both, and click **Save caps**.

* Leave a cap blank for no limit on that window.
* Both caps apply at the same time. An organization's usage is refused once either cap is reached, until that window resets.
* A cap of \$0 refuses the organization's requests billed to the account until you raise or clear the cap.

Changes take effect immediately. Raising or clearing a cap admits the organization's next request. Lowering a cap below the organization's current window usage refuses its next request until the window resets.


# Identity and access
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access

Verify domains, connect single sign-on and SCIM, write the routing rules that place people in organizations, and look up what a sign-in error page means.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators who connect the deployment to their agency's identity provider and control which organization each person belongs to.

Identity and access are configured once here and shared by every organization in your tenant.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These cases are covered on other pages:
>
> * **Setting up a new tenant**: see [Tenant setup wizard](/docs/government/tenant-admin/setup-wizard)
> * **Mapping directory groups to seat tiers and roles**: see [Group mappings](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning)

## Domains

Claude for Government routes users to your tenant by the domain of their email address, so at least one domain must be verified before members can sign in. While Anthropic is finishing initial setup of your tenant, or if Anthropic has deactivated it, sign-in is disabled for everyone, and only Anthropic can change that. Once a tenant administrator can sign in, that setup is finished.

Your tenant can have more than one domain, and a verified domain can belong to only one tenant. However many domains are verified here, your tenant has one set of [admin portals](/docs/government/tenant-admin/overview#tenants-and-organizations), and the [routing rules](#routing-rules) decide which organization each person joins.

Domains that Anthropic registered on your behalf during onboarding are already verified. To add one yourself, enter the domain in the **Claim a domain** field and click **Claim**. You will be shown a DNS TXT record to publish on that domain; once the record is live, click **Verify now** and the domain becomes active.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Verify the domain of your own email address first, if your agency owns it. Once your tenant has a verified domain, you can't start sign-in or get the [emailed sign-in link](#emailed-sign-in-link) by entering an address on an unverified domain.

* **Verification delay.** DNS changes take time to propagate, so try again shortly if verification does not succeed on the first attempt.
* **After verification.** Keep the DNS TXT record in place while you are using Claude for Government.
* **Subdomains.** A subdomain is a separate domain, so verifying `example.gov` doesn't cover email addresses at `sub.example.gov`.
* **Removal.** To withdraw an unverified claim, click **Withdraw** next to it. To remove a verified domain, contact Anthropic.

## Single sign-on

Members sign in through your agency's identity provider (for example, Microsoft Entra, Okta, or ADFS), which needs to support SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC). You need at least one [verified domain](#domains) before you can connect single sign-on.

You register Claude for Government as an application in your identity provider, then enter your provider's connection details here. Once connected, sign-ins are redirected to your provider. A second sign-in from the same browser within a few minutes, such as connecting Claude Desktop right after signing in on the web, may not be redirected again.

Only one protocol is active at a time. Use the **OIDC** and **SAML** tabs to switch between the two forms; saving one replaces the other.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Saving a new single sign-on configuration takes effect immediately and applies to everyone, including you. After saving, select **Test sign-in** to check the connection with your own account while you stay signed in. If single sign-on fails, Primary Owners and tenant administrators can use the [emailed sign-in link](#emailed-sign-in-link).

### Register in your identity provider

Copy the following values from the card into your identity provider when you create the application there:

* **Redirect URI / ACS URL** is where your identity provider sends the user back after authentication. The same value is used whether you choose OIDC (where it's called the Redirect URI) or SAML (where it's called the Assertion Consumer Service URL).
* **SP Entity ID / Audience** is the unique identifier your identity provider uses to recognize this application. Providers label this field differently; it may appear as Identifier, Entity ID, or Audience URI.

For SAML, **More values your IdP may ask for** lists the remaining details some providers request. After you save a SAML connection, an **SP metadata URL** appears alongside these values.

### Connect with OIDC

If your identity provider supports OpenID Connect, fill in the OIDC section:

* **Client ID** is the application ID your identity provider assigned when you registered the app.
* **Client secret** is the secret your identity provider generated for that application. It is stored securely and never shown again after you save.
* **Authorization URL**, **Token URL**, **Issuer**, and **JWKS URL** are your identity provider's OIDC endpoints. Copy them exactly from your provider's OpenID Connect discovery document, whose address ends in `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. For Microsoft Entra, the Issuer ends in `/v2.0`.

### Connect with SAML

If your identity provider uses SAML, fill in the SAML section instead. Your provider must sign the SAML assertion, not only the response.

* **IdP metadata XML** is the federation metadata document for your identity provider. Download the XML file from your provider and paste the full document into the field. The metadata is read from what you paste; it is never fetched from a URL. When your identity provider rotates its signing certificate, download the new metadata XML, paste it into the **IdP metadata XML** field, and click the **Update** button.

Once SAML is active, the card shows the Entity ID and SSO URL extracted from your metadata so you can confirm the connection is pointing where you expect.

### Attribute mapping (advanced)

Open the **Attribute mapping** panel in the OIDC or SAML section if the email, first-name, or last-name fields arrive under different names than the defaults. For OIDC the defaults are the standard `email`, `given_name`, and `family_name` claims; for SAML the email default covers the common attribute names, and the name defaults are `firstName` and `lastName`.

Claude for Government identifies a person at single sign-on from what your identity provider returns, not from the email address they type, so typing an alias doesn't create a second account. A separate identity in your identity provider that has its own email address gets its own account when your [routing rules](#routing-rules) place it.

### Where sign-in starts

People start sign-in from a Claude app, such as Claude Desktop (**Sign in with your organization**), or from the web portal in a browser, and Claude for Government then sends them to your identity provider. Starting from the application's tile in your provider's app portal (such as Microsoft My Apps), or from a sign-in test in your provider's admin console, is not supported.

### Emailed sign-in link

There is no local break-glass account or stored password. Primary Owners and [tenant administrators](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins) can sign in to the web portal without single sign-on, whether or not it is connected: they request a single-use link with **Email me a sign-in link** on the web portal's sign-in page.

Until your tenant has a verified domain, only tenant administrators can get a link. Once it has one, a link is sent only to an active Primary Owner or tenant administrator whose address is exactly on one of your tenant's [verified domains](#domains). One person can get at most five links an hour. The page that follows reads the same whether or not a link is sent.

## SCIM provisioning

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Directory sync (SCIM) and group mappings" />

Video: Directory sync (SCIM) and group mappings (2 min 3 s). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

[Transcript](/docs/government/video-walkthroughs#directory-sync-scim-and-group-mappings)

SCIM is the standard protocol identity providers use to push users and groups to a connected service automatically, so that accounts are created, updated, and deactivated in step with your agency's directory. Connecting SCIM is optional; without it, users are created the first time they sign in. With SCIM connected, a person your directory has never sent still gets an account the first time they sign in, if a [sign-in rule](#sign-in-rules) covers them. People join your tenant by signing in or through your directory.

[Provisioning rules](#provisioning-rules-scim), [group mappings](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning), and [group-specific settings](/docs/government/config/overview#group-specific-settings) need SCIM, because they act on the [directory groups](#directory-groups) your identity provider pushes. Model access and usage limits come from each person's [seat tier](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers), which an organization owner can assign on the [Users](/docs/government/org-admin/users) page without SCIM.

### Connect your directory

SCIM provisioning is configured entirely from this page, with no action needed from Anthropic. You need at least one [verified domain](#domains) before you can generate a SCIM token.

* **SCIM base URL** is the address your identity provider pushes user and group updates to. You'll paste this value into your identity provider's provisioning settings, where Microsoft Entra calls it the *Tenant URL* and Okta calls it the *SCIM connector base URL*.
* **SCIM secret token.** Your identity provider authenticates to the SCIM address with a bearer token that you generate here. Click **Generate token** to create one, then paste the value into your identity provider's *Secret Token* (or equivalent) field.

> [!WARNING]
>
> The full token value is shown **only once**, immediately after you create it. Copy it into your identity provider before clicking Done. If you lose the value, generate a new token and revoke the old one.

Afterward the token table shows only a short hint (the last few characters) of each token. You can keep more than one token active at a time, which lets you rotate without an outage: generate a new token, update your identity provider to use it, confirm a sync succeeds, and then revoke the old one. Revoking a token takes effect immediately.

### Existing accounts when you connect SCIM

Connecting SCIM keeps existing accounts. A directory entry links to the account with the same email address when a [provisioning rule](#provisioning-rules-scim) names that person's organization, or at the latest at their next sign-in once they are in an organization. There is no need to delete an account first. A deactivation in your directory reaches the account once it is linked. Until then, your directory's request to deactivate, delete, or change the email address of that user is refused with a 409 error. Have your directory resend it once the account is linked.

Have your identity provider send, as the primary SCIM email, the address each person signs in with. A new entry with a different address creates a second account once a provisioning rule places it, and a deactivation in your directory doesn't reach the account they use. For users managed by your directory, the email address shown in Claude for Government is kept in step with your directory, and the sign-in token's email is ignored.

### Directory groups

Once your identity provider has pushed groups over SCIM, they appear here with their member counts. The order you set here is the priority used for group-level configuration on the [Config](/docs/government/config/overview#group-specific-settings) page and for [seat-tier mappings](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#how-mappings-are-applied). Reordering groups can change the seat tier of members who belong to more than one group mapped to a seat tier in their organization, without waiting for the next directory sync.

## Routing rules

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Organizations, seats, and routing rules" />

Video: Organizations, seats, and routing rules (2 min 14 s). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

[Transcript](/docs/government/video-walkthroughs#organizations-seats-and-routing-rules)

A **routing rule** is an instruction of the form "if a person matches this condition, place them in this organization." A new person whom no routing rule matches is refused: there is no default organization and no fallback. To send people to an organization by group, use a [provisioning rule](#provisioning-rules-scim) rather than the identity provider group rule shown in the video. Before you remove or reorder a sign-in rule, read [When rules move people](#when-rules-move-people).

Before any rule runs, the sign-in flow first checks that the person's email domain is one of your tenant's [**verified domains**](#domains). An address outside your verified domains never reaches your tenant at all, regardless of what rules you've written.

A person can arrive by signing in or through your directory, and each way has its own rule list:

* **Sign-in rules** run each time a person signs in.
* **Provisioning rules** run when your directory creates or updates someone through SCIM. They match on synced directory groups, and a change takes effect after you save it, without waiting for the next directory sync.

Until at least one rule is added, no new person can sign in, and a banner on the page says that no routing rules are configured.

### Sign-in rules

An **email domain** rule matches the domain of the user's email address exactly. You choose from your tenant's verified domains; you cannot type an arbitrary domain.

To place people by **group**, use a [provisioning rule](#provisioning-rules-scim).

Rules are evaluated from top to bottom, and the first match wins. Only one rule can exist for any given condition. Each rule shows a status line with diagnostics:

* **Last matched** (or **Never matched**) tells you when the rule most recently matched someone.
* A **target deactivated** badge means the rule points at an organization that has been deactivated. The rule is skipped during evaluation.
* A **stale value** badge means the condition refers to something that no longer exists, such as a domain removed from your verified list. The rule is skipped during evaluation.

### Provisioning rules (SCIM)

The console shows this section once SCIM is connected. Provisioning rules match on **directory groups** that your identity provider has synced, and decide which organization a user is placed in when your directory provisions or updates them. You choose groups from the synced list; a group that hasn't synced yet won't appear in the picker.

Provisioning rules work the same way as sign-in rules: they're an ordered list, the first match wins, and only one rule can exist per group. Adding, reordering, or removing provisioning rules can move already-placed users.

A provisioning rule doesn't place an account that is in no organization. Your tenant's first administrator starts that way, able to use the admin portal but not Claude. A [sign-in rule](#sign-in-rules) for their email domain does place them, but it applies to everyone on that domain who signs in while it exists. A person with no account gets one in the rule's organization. A member of another organization whom your directory doesn't manage [moves to it](#when-rules-move-people). Removing the rule undoes neither. So add the rule, have the administrator sign out and back in, then remove it. Or contact Anthropic to place them.

### Add and remove rules

To add a rule, choose the match type (for sign-in rules), pick the value, choose the target organization, and click **Add rule**. New rules are added at the bottom of the list; reorder after adding if you need a different priority. To remove a rule, click **Remove** next to it and confirm.

### When rules move people

A move ends the person's active sessions. It does not revoke a [Compliance API key](/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api) they created. They lose their seat and role in the organization they leave, join the new one as a User or in the role its group mappings give them, and are reseated according to its available seats. Their account itself is kept. Because the Claude desktop app stores conversations on each person's own device, a move does not affect desktop chat history. See [Data storage and retention](/docs/government/security/security-and-data-handling#data-storage-and-retention).

Because sign-in rules run every time, a rule change has these effects on people who already exist:

* If a person now matches a rule that points to a different organization, they are moved on their next sign-in, unless another case in this list applies.
* If a person is a [Primary Owner](/docs/government/org-admin/users#understanding-roles) of their organization, they are moved only when they are also a [tenant administrator](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins) and that organization has another active Primary Owner.
* Removing an identity provider group rule (listed as **Anyone with IdP group**), or moving it lower, can move people already in its organization at their next sign-in.
* If a person no longer matches any rule (for example, you removed the only rule that covered them), they keep their current organization and can still sign in. The no-match refusal applies only to people who have no account yet.
* If a person's account is managed by your directory (that is, it was created or linked through SCIM), sign-in rules do **not** move them. Directory-managed accounts are moved only by provisioning rules.

## When someone cannot sign in

### Preview routing

Enter an email address to see how that person would be routed, without changing anything. For a person who already has an account, the preview shows which rule matches them, not [whether they are moved or refused](#when-rules-move-people).

The result lists the rules in order with the outcome for each, for sign-in and, when SCIM is connected, for directory provisioning.

### Unplaced users

* **Rejected sign-ins** lists people who tried to sign in and were turned away, for example because no rule matched them. Each entry shows who tried and when. These records are kept so you can see who's trying and failing to get in. Click **Test in preview** to load that person's email into the preview. Click **Clear** to delete the record, or **Clear all** to remove every entry. Clearing does not block the person; a fresh entry appears if they are refused again.
* **Synced, not routed**, in the **Provisioning rules (SCIM)** section, lists directory entries not yet linked to an account. A new person here can sign in once a sign-in rule covers them or a provisioning rule places them. Someone who already has an account keeps signing in. To place the people in a group, add a provisioning rule that covers it. If someone in the group already has an account in another organization, the rule can [move them](#when-rules-move-people), unless they are a Primary Owner. The rule doesn't place an [account in no organization](#accounts-in-no-organization). People on a domain you haven't verified aren't placed, and people whose mapped tier has no free seats wait for one, as described under [How mappings are applied](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning#how-mappings-are-applied).

Once a person is placed, their entries in these lists are cleaned up automatically.

### Sign-in error pages

The table shows what a person may see when sign-in fails, and what to do about it.

| What the person sees | What it means | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| "We couldn't find an organization for that email." | The address's domain is not a verified domain of any active tenant. Until Anthropic finishes setting up your tenant, everyone sees this | Verify the domain under [Domains](#domains). If no administrator can sign in, contact your Anthropic representative |
| "Single sign-on isn't configured for your organization yet." | The domain is verified, but no identity provider is connected | Connect [single sign-on](#single-sign-on). Primary Owners and tenant administrators can use the [emailed link](#emailed-sign-in-link) |
| **Almost there** | Your identity provider signed them in, but no routing rule matched, or the rule's organization is deactivated | Find them under **Rejected sign-ins** and add a [rule](#routing-rules) that covers them |
| **Signed in with a different account** | Your identity provider returned another address than the one they typed | They can continue as the returned address. If sign-in then finds no organization, verify that address's domain, or correct the address your provider sends |
| **Email address missing** | Your identity provider didn't send an email address | Add an email attribute or claim in your identity provider, or name it under [Attribute mapping](#attribute-mapping-advanced) |
| **Account deactivated** | Their account or directory entry is deactivated | Reactivate them in your directory: see [Deactivated users](/docs/government/org-admin/users#deactivated-users). If your directory doesn't manage them, contact your Anthropic representative |
| "Invalid signature in response from identity provider" | Your provider doesn't sign the assertion (required once you save the SAML section), or its signing certificate expired or isn't the one in your saved metadata | For an unsigned assertion, set your provider to sign it; no change is needed in Claude for Government. Otherwise renew the certificate if it expired, then paste the new metadata under [Connect with SAML](#connect-with-saml) |
| "Login timeout. Please sign in again." | A SAML response that arrives outside its validity period, or names the wrong audience, can produce this page right after the person signs in at your provider | Check the clock on each identity provider server you run, and set the audience in your provider to your [**SP Entity ID / Audience**](#register-in-your-identity-provider) |
| **Sign-in not completed** | The sign-in was canceled, or the exchange with your identity provider failed | Run **Test sign-in**, which names the likely cause |


# Organizations
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/organizations

See every organization in your tenant, open an organization's admin view, add an organization and get it ready for people, and copy user email addresses.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators who create and oversee the organizations within their agency's deployment.

## How organizations work

An **organization** is a workspace that holds a set of users, a set of seats, its own spend caps, and its own product settings. A user never belongs to more than one organization at a time, and each organization is linked to exactly one **billing account** (the credit and seat pool that funds it). Organizations share the tenant's sign-in and provisioning setup.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Which organization a user joins isn't controlled on this page. You set that with the routing rules on the [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access) page.

## The organization list

Clicking an organization's name opens its organization admin view. When you do this you are acting as an Owner of that organization and can manage its users, seats, and settings. Unless the organization [manages its own billing account](/docs/government/org-admin/billing#seats), you can also grant or remove its [Primary Owner role](/docs/government/org-admin/users#understanding-roles) on its Users page.

To email everyone in your tenant, or in one organization, click **Copy user email addresses** at the top of the page. The page that opens lists the email addresses of everyone except deactivated users, for the whole tenant and for each organization.

## Adding an organization

Expand the **Add organization** section to create a new organization. You'll provide the following:

* **Name** is what the organization will be called. To rename an organization, contact Anthropic.
* **Primary Owner email** is the email address of the person who will be the new organization's first administrator. This person becomes the Primary Owner and can immediately manage the organization's users and settings. Choose someone on one of your verified domains who has no active account in your tenant yet. No invitation is sent, so let them know. They do **not** become a tenant administrator; tenant-level access is granted separately on the [Admins](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins) page.
* **Billing account** determines where the organization's credits and seats come from. Choose an existing billing account from the list; the new organization draws from that account's credit balance and seat pool alongside any other organizations already on it. Only billing accounts that are active and tenant-managed appear in the list. If the list is empty, contact Anthropic to have one set up.

### After you add an organization

The new organization appears in the list immediately and you can click through to its organization admin view. Before people can use it:

* Add a routing rule on the [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access) page so that the right people are placed in the new organization when they sign in or are provisioned. Until a rule targets the new organization, nobody will land there automatically.
* Give it seats on the [Seats](/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats) page. If its billing account has no pool of seats, it needs [a seat tier of its own](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#creating-a-self-managed-tier) instead. A newly created organization starts with no seats distributed to it, so its Primary Owner has no seat tier and cannot use Claude yet. Saving the organization's first seats also seats the Primary Owner, and anyone else already in it without a seat tier, automatically.
* If you want to limit how much the new organization can spend from its billing account, set a spend cap on it on the [Billing](/docs/government/tenant-admin/credits) page. With no cap, the account's balance is the only limit.

## Deactivating an organization

You cannot delete an organization from this page. If an organization is no longer needed, contact Anthropic to have it deactivated. Routing rules that target a deactivated organization stop matching. The users still in it are deactivated with it and cannot sign in. Reactivating the organization later does not necessarily reactivate them.


# Tenant administration
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/overview

Manage the settings that apply across your whole agency: organizations, identity and sign-in, and how seats are distributed and spend caps are set.

> **Who this portal is for:** Tenant administrators who manage their agency's overall Claude for Government deployment across every organization. If you manage a single organization, see the [Organization administration](/docs/government/org-admin/overview) guide instead.

The tenant admin portal is where you manage the things that apply across every team using the service: identity, organization routing, seats, spend caps, and tenant-wide product settings.

## Tenants and organizations

For how your tenant, its organizations, and billing accounts fit together, see [How your deployment is organized](/docs/government/overview#how-your-deployment-is-organized).

The [**organization admin**](/docs/government/org-admin/overview#who-can-access-it) portal is where each organization's own owners manage that organization's users, seats, and settings. As a tenant administrator, you can open any organization's admin view from the [Organizations](/docs/government/tenant-admin/organizations) page, or you can use the **Switch to org view** link at the bottom of every tenant admin page.

## Who can use this portal

Only **tenant administrators** can open the tenant admin portal. Tenant administrators are a specific list of people that are managed on the [Admins](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins) page, and this list is separate from any role someone holds inside an organization. If you need tenant-level access, ask an existing tenant administrator to add you on the [Admins](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins) page.

## Getting set up for the first time

The [setup wizard](/docs/government/tenant-admin/setup-wizard) walks you through setting up a new tenant step by step. You reach it through the **Resume setup** banner that appears above the navigation until your tenant is fully set up. Add at least one more tenant administrator on the [Admins](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins) page so that you are not the only person with tenant-level access.

## Pages in this portal

* **[Organizations](/docs/government/tenant-admin/organizations)**: see every organization in your tenant, open any organization's admin view, and create new organizations
* **[Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access)**: connect [single sign-on](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#single-sign-on), manage the [SCIM provisioning](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#scim-provisioning) token, write the [routing rules](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#routing-rules) that place users into organizations, and find out [why someone cannot sign in](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#when-someone-cannot-sign-in)
* **[Seats](/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats)**: distribute the seats in each billing account's pool to the organizations that account funds
* **[Billing](/docs/government/tenant-admin/credits)**: see each billing account's balance and set spend caps that limit how much each organization can draw from it
* **[Readiness](/docs/government/tenant-admin/readiness)**: see what is blocking your organizations from using Claude and where each item is resolved
* **[Config](/docs/government/tenant-admin/configuration)**: set product settings that apply to every organization, and optionally lock them so organizations can't override them
* **[Admins](/docs/government/tenant-admin/admins)**: manage who has access to this tenant admin portal
* **[Compliance API keys](/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api)**: create and revoke API keys that stream audit events for every organization in your tenant, together with tenant-level activity, to a SIEM or log management system

Some tabs, such as **Billing** and **Compliance API keys**, appear in the navigation only when they are available to your tenant.


# Readiness
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/readiness

Readiness checks for your tenant and its organizations: what the checks on domains, routing rules, sign-in failures, and billing mean, and who clears them.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators who are setting up a deployment, or who need to find out why users in any organization are unable to use Claude.

The **Readiness** page shows what is blocking your organizations from using Claude and where each item is resolved. To open it, go to **Settings > Readiness** in the tenant admin portal. You would normally work through it once during initial setup and then return whenever the **Settings** menu shows a notification dot. The dot means a required step is unfinished.

In each checklist, the first unfinished required step shows why it is blocked, and either offers a button that takes you to the page where the fix is made or names who it is waiting on, such as **Waiting on Anthropic**. A step that isn't required doesn't raise the dot, but people can still be stuck until it is done.

When a step is something only Anthropic can do, such as adding credits or reactivating an organization, contact your Anthropic representative to move it forward.

## Tenant-level checks

These checks cover the things every organization in your tenant depends on. The table shows what a check means when it is unfinished, and who can clear it.

| Check | What it means | Who clears it |
| - | - | - |
| **Register a domain** | Until at least one domain is verified, only tenant administrators can sign in, by [emailed link](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#emailed-sign-in-link). | You, under [Domains](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#domains) |
| **Add a routing rule** | Until at least one rule points at an active organization, people who don't yet have an account are turned away. | You, under [Routing rules](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#routing-rules). If your tenant has no active organization, create one on the [Organizations](/docs/government/tenant-admin/organizations) page first |
| **Fund the billing account** | No billing account linked to an active organization has a positive balance. | Funding is arranged with Anthropic |
| **Configure the seat pool** | No billing account has a seat pool yet, so the [Seats](/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats) page has no seats on Anthropic-managed tiers for you to distribute. Organizations can still give their users seats on any [self-managed seat tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) they create themselves. | The pool is configured by Anthropic |
| **Set up SCIM provisioning** | No directory is connected. Connecting one is optional. | You, under [SCIM provisioning](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#scim-provisioning) |
| **Review sign-in failures** | People tried to sign in and were turned away. | You, under [Unplaced users](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#unplaced-users) |
| **Fix the identity provider's email attribute** | Sign-in attempts were refused because your identity provider didn't send an email address. | You, in your identity provider's sign-in configuration or under [Attribute mapping](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#attribute-mapping-advanced) |

If your tenant has a single active organization, checks from [that organization's Readiness page](/docs/government/org-admin/readiness#what-the-checks-mean) appear in the same list.

**Connect single sign-on** shows only on the [setup wizard](/docs/government/tenant-admin/setup-wizard)'s Finish step. Until you connect it under [Single sign-on](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#single-sign-on), only Primary Owners and tenant administrators can sign in, by [emailed link](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#emailed-sign-in-link).

## Organizations

When your tenant has more than one active organization, a card lists each one as **Ready** or with the step that blocks it.

Expanding a row loads that organization's full checklist inline. The steps are the same ones described on the [organization Readiness page](/docs/government/org-admin/readiness), and any buttons you click here act on that organization, not the one you are currently viewing in the organization admin portal.

Deactivated organizations appear here with their reactivation status. An organization whose billing account is retired must be assigned a new one by Anthropic before it can be reactivated.


# Seats
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats

Divide each billing account's seat pool among the organizations it funds, and see who can change an allocation and why a change is refused.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators who distribute purchased seats to the organizations in their deployment.

## How seats are organized

A **seat** is what entitles one person to use Claude. Every seat belongs to a [**seat tier**](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#the-tier-list).

Anthropic sets up your [billing accounts](/docs/government/tenant-admin/credits#how-billing-works). Each organization must be linked to exactly one, and several can share one. If an account has a pool of seats, you divide it on this page among the organizations it funds. Organization owners then assign seat tiers to users individually or by [directory group](/docs/government/org-admin/provisioning). Organizations that [create their own seat tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers#creating-a-self-managed-tier) don't need a pool.

If you need more seats in a pool, or a new tier added to it, contact Anthropic.

## Change seat allocations

On the **Seats** page in the tenant admin portal, edit the number fields under an organization's name and click its **Save**. Changes take effect immediately.

The save is rejected in cases such as these:

* The account's organizations would together hold more seats than the pool has for a tier.
* You try to reduce a tier below the number of people already seated on it in that organization. Ask the organization's owners to unassign people from that tier first, then reduce the allocation.

To move seats between organizations on the same billing account, lower one and raise the other. If no seats remain in the pool, save the reduction first, then the increase.

If an account says **Managed by** an organization's administrators, that organization's [Primary Owners](/docs/government/org-admin/users#understanding-roles) manage its seats.

## How seats affect new users

A new person placed in an organization (by a routing rule on the [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access) page) can be given a seat automatically: see [How seats are assigned automatically](/docs/government/org-admin/seats#how-seats-are-assigned-automatically).


# Tenant setup wizard
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/setup-wizard

Set up a new tenant in order: verify a domain, connect single sign-on, add an organization, give it seats, and add the routing rule that lets people sign in.

> **Who this is for:** Tenant administrators who have just been given access to a new Claude for Government deployment and need to get it ready for the rest of their agency.

The setup wizard walks you through the things that need to be in place before everyone else can use Claude: a verified email domain, a connection to your identity provider, at least one organization, seats for that organization, and a routing rule that places people in it.

Before single sign-on is connected, you sign in with a single-use link that the sign-in page emails to you on request. See [Emailed sign-in link](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#emailed-sign-in-link). Until the required steps are complete, a **Resume setup** banner appears at the top of the tenant admin pages, and its button opens the wizard. If you land in another view, use the footer links to reach the tenant view.

Every step in the wizard edits the same settings as the matching page in the full admin portal. You can leave the wizard at any point using **Continue later**.

## Wizard steps

### Welcome step

The first step is a read-only summary of what Anthropic has already set up for you. If a detail looks wrong (for example, the tenant name is misspelled), contact Anthropic before going further, because the tenant name cannot be changed from the portal.

### Domains step

<video aria-label="Video walkthrough: Verify your domain and connect single sign-on" />

Video: Verify your domain and connect single sign-on (2 min 24 s). Narrated with an AI-generated voice, with on-screen captions.

[Transcript](/docs/government/video-walkthroughs#verify-your-domain-and-connect-single-sign-on)

The video also covers the Single sign-on step. For later steps, see [Video walkthroughs](/docs/government/video-walkthroughs#admin-series).

Claude for Government looks at the domain of a person's email address to decide which tenant they belong to, so at least one verified domain must be registered before anyone else can sign in. If Anthropic already verified the domain you plan to use, you can move straight on to the next step. To add another domain, see [Domains](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#domains), and read its warning first, so that you can still sign in.

### Single sign-on step

Until single sign-on is connected, only tenant administrators and Primary Owners can sign in, by [emailed link](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#emailed-sign-in-link). The full field reference for both protocols is on the [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#single-sign-on) page.

Once single sign-on is connected, people [sign in from a Claude app or the web portal](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#where-sign-in-starts), and Claude for Government sends them to your provider from there. After connecting, use **Test sign-in** on this step to check that it works.

### Provisioning step

This step is optional, though highly recommended. If your identity provider supports SCIM, you can connect it here so that accounts are created automatically. To connect it, see [SCIM provisioning](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#scim-provisioning). This step labels the SCIM base URL **Tenant URL**.

You do not have to finish the provider-side setup before moving on. Once your provider has pushed at least one group, you can add provisioning rules that place people by group membership on the [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#provisioning-rules-scim) page.

### Organizations step

You need at least one organization before you can route anyone anywhere. If Anthropic already created one, this step lists it and you can move on. To add one, fill in the **Add organization** form, described under [Adding an organization](/docs/government/tenant-admin/organizations#adding-an-organization). For **Primary Owner email**, choose someone on one of your verified domains who has no active account in your tenant yet. No invitation is sent, so let them know.

### Seats and spend caps step

This step lets you give each organization seats and, optionally, a spend cap. It shows a seat-count field for the first seat tier. For per-tier control, use the full [Seats](/docs/government/tenant-admin/seats) page after setup. If the step says there are no seats to distribute, continue. Each organization then needs [a seat tier of its own](#seat-tiers-and-products-steps) before its members can use Claude. You can adjust caps later from the tenant [Billing](/docs/government/tenant-admin/credits) page.

### Routing step

Routing rules decide which organization a person lands in when they sign in. A new person who does not match any rule cannot sign in at all, so you need at least one rule that covers your users. A single rule that maps your main email domain to your main organization is enough to get started. To add one, use the form:

* In the **If** field, choose **Anyone with email domain**, and in the second field pick the domain.
* In the **Then place in** field, pick the organization.
* Click **Add rule**.

A domain rule that covers your own address places you in that organization too, as a User, at your next sign-in. You keep tenant administration. If no domain rule covers your address, see [how to join an organization yourself](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#accounts-in-no-organization).

Rules that match directory groups pushed over SCIM are managed on the full [Identity and access](/docs/government/tenant-admin/identity-and-access#routing-rules) page, which also has a preview tool for testing where a specific email address would land.

### Seat tiers and Products steps

Unless your tenant has more than one organization, the wizard includes the **Seat tiers** and **Products** steps. In a tenant with more than one organization, each organization's owner completes them in their own [organization setup wizard](/docs/government/org-admin/setup-wizard), which describes both. The optional **Products** step sets which Claude products your members can sign in to, such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Claude for Microsoft 365.

Seat tiers set each person's spend limits. To [see or change your seat tiers](/docs/government/org-admin/seat-tiers) after setup, select **Switch to org view** in the page footer and go to **People > Tiers**.

### Finish step

The last step shows a live readiness checklist. For what the checks mean, see [Readiness](/docs/government/tenant-admin/readiness#tenant-level-checks). **Connect single sign-on** isn't a required step, but members can't sign in until you connect it.

The wizard reads the live state of your tenant, so if something changes later (for example, you remove your only routing rule), the **Resume setup** banner reappears on the tenant admin pages until the checklist is satisfied again.


# Tenant restrictions
Source: https://claude.com/docs/government/tenant-admin/tenant-restrictions

Restrict which Claude for Government tenants can be reached from your agency's network by having your network proxy inject an allowlist header.

> **Who this is for:** IT and network administrators who operate their agency's outbound web proxy or secure web gateway and want to prevent users on that network from signing in to Claude for Government with a different agency's account.

Tenant restrictions let you limit which Claude for Government tenants can be reached from your network. Your network appliance adds a header to every outbound request listing the tenants you allow, and Claude for Government refuses any request that authenticates as a tenant not on that list.

This is useful when people on your network may hold accounts in more than one agency's tenant (for example, a contractor who supports several agencies) and you need to ensure that work done from your network stays within your own tenant.

There is nothing to enable on the Claude for Government side. The restriction is activated entirely by the presence of the header on the request, so it takes effect the moment your proxy begins injecting it and only for traffic that passes through that proxy.

## How it works

Your agency's network appliance (a forward proxy, secure web gateway, or similar device that can inspect and modify HTTPS traffic) injects an `Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids` header on every request it forwards to Claude for Government. The header value is a comma-separated list of tenant IDs.

On each request, Claude for Government compares the authenticated user's tenant against the list in the header. When the header is present and the user's tenant is not on the list, the request is refused. When the header is absent, no restriction applies.

The check covers every way a user can reach Claude for Government:

* The web application, including the tenant and organization admin portals
* The desktop application
* Claude Code
* The Claude for Microsoft 365 add-ins
* Direct API calls
* SCIM directory provisioning and the [Compliance API](/docs/government/org-admin/compliance-api)

The same check applies at sign-in, so a user signing in to a tenant that is not on the list sees the refusal at the sign-in screen rather than after authentication completes.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A tenant restriction can only narrow access. A user still needs valid credentials for a tenant on the list; the header never grants access to a tenant the user does not already belong to.

## Configure your network proxy

Configure your appliance to do both of the following on every request to your Claude for Government domains:

1. **Remove** any `Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids` header that arrived from the client.
2. **Set** a single `Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids` header to your allowlist value.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Your appliance must remove the incoming header before setting its own. If the appliance only appends, ordinary traffic still works, so the misconfiguration is not obvious. A client that supplies its own value can then reach the server with both values, which either bypasses the restriction or causes that client's requests to fail, depending on how the appliance merges the two. Most secure web gateway products have a distinct "set" or "overwrite" action that removes and replaces in one step; use that rather than "append" or "add".

Apply the rule to requests for the Claude for Government domains provided to you during onboarding, as well as your agency's own custom domain if you have one. Because Claude for Government is served over HTTPS, your appliance must perform TLS inspection for these hosts so that it can add the header to the encrypted request.

Requests that do not pass through your appliance (for example, from a device that is off your network) do not carry the header and are not restricted. Pair this feature with your existing controls that ensure managed devices route through the appliance.

## Header format

The header name is `Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids`. Header names are not case-sensitive, so your appliance may send the name in any casing.

The value is one or more tenant IDs separated by commas. A tenant ID has the form `umb_` followed by a lowercase UUID with dashes. The `umb_` prefix is optional, and whitespace around each ID is ignored. The UUID must be lowercase; an uppercase or mixed-case value is rejected as invalid.

```text theme={null}
Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids: umb_00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```

For more than one tenant, separate the IDs with commas:

```text theme={null}
Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids: umb_00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000, umb_11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```

### Finding your tenant ID

Anthropic provides your tenant ID during onboarding. If you do not have it on hand, contact Anthropic support and ask for the tenant ID for your deployment.

## What a blocked user sees

A user who tries to sign in to a tenant that is not on your allowlist sees a refusal page titled **This account isn't permitted from this network**, with guidance to sign in with an authorized account or contact their IT administrator.

A user who is already signed in when the restriction takes effect, or whose application makes a request in the background, receives an error in the product reading **Your organization restricts which accounts can be used from this network. Contact your IT administrator.** Direct API calls return HTTP 403 with the error code `tenant_restriction_violation` and the message `Access restricted by network policy. Contact your IT administrator.`

The refusal does not tell the user which tenants are permitted. Keep a record of your allowlist alongside your proxy configuration so that your help desk can answer user questions without inspecting the appliance.

## How invalid headers are handled

Claude for Government rejects malformed headers so that a misconfigured proxy fails visibly rather than silently allowing everything through. A request is rejected with HTTP 400 and the error code `tenant_restriction_header_invalid` when any of the following is true:

* The header is present but empty, or contains only whitespace or commas.
* Any value in the list is not a valid tenant ID.
* The list contains more than 64 tenant IDs.
* The request carries more than one `Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids` header.

A request with no `Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids` header at all is not restricted.

## Verifying the configuration

You can confirm the restriction is working before rolling it out broadly.

To confirm a block, temporarily set the proxy's allowlist to a tenant ID you do not own (any validly formatted ID works), then sign in to your own tenant from a browser that routes through the proxy. You should see the **This account isn't permitted from this network** refusal page. A direct API request in the same configuration should return HTTP 403 with the error code `tenant_restriction_violation`.

To confirm normal access, set the proxy's allowlist to your real tenant ID and repeat the request. It should succeed.

To confirm the appliance is overwriting rather than appending, have the test client send its own `Anthropic-Allowed-Tenant-Ids` header with your real tenant ID while the proxy's allowlist is set to an ID you do not own. The request should still return 403 (the proxy's value wins), not 400 (two headers reached the server) or 200 (the client's value reached the server).

## Things to know

* Personal Claude accounts use `claude.ai`, which is a separate host from the Claude for Government service. A personal account cannot sign in to Claude for Government, and a Claude for Government account cannot sign in to `claude.ai`. The header-based restriction on this page applies only to Claude for Government traffic; it does not govern access to `claude.ai`.

> Once a rule covers them, they are placed in its organization, and the list clears on its own.
>
> In the organization's admin view, People now includes Group mappings. Map claude-users to a seat tier, here Standard, and claude-owners to the Owner role.
>
> On Users, the provisioned members now hold their mapped seat tier and role.
>
> While sync is connected, your directory is the source of truth. Change groups in your provider, because role or seat tier edits made by hand are overwritten by the group mappings.

### Verify a managed device and spot common failures

What a correctly managed device shows, and the usual causes of an empty model picker, a claude.ai sign-in screen, a repeated settings prompt, and an expired session. >
